sections.title: 2. Who the exam is for
sections.html:
As a candidate for this exam, you’re a functional consultant with customer service expertise. You’re responsible for implementing solutions that focus upon:

  • Customer service
  • Quality
  • Reliability
  • Efficiency
  • Customer satisfaction

You design and implement service management processes and automation in collaboration with solution architects and developers. You coordinate with customer engagement administrators to implement and upgrade customer service components including:

  • Case management
  • Dynamics 365 Copilot in Service
  • Collaboration
  • Knowledge management
  • Customer feedback

You must have strong applied knowledge of customer service, including in-depth understanding of cases, knowledge management, queues, service-level agreements (SLAs), Customer Service applications, Customer Voice, and routing.

As a functional consultant, your knowledge should include:

  • Comprehensive understanding of the customer service application's role in relation to the Dynamics 365 suite of apps.
  • Basic understanding of the solution architecture.

Source: Official study guide (audience profile), updated 2026-02-09.

sections.title: 4. How to read the skills measured
sections.html:
• The bullets illustrate how a skill is assessed; related topics may appear (Microsoft's own note in the study guide). Treat each bullet as a heading for everything around it.
  • Most questions cover generally available (GA) features, but Preview features can appear when they are commonly used. Where the documentation labels something preview, retired or renamed, this guide says so.
  • Expect scenario questions (pick the right setting, path, role or sequence for a requirement) and decision questions (X versus Y). Exact names, menu paths and limits matter.
  • Case studies present a business scenario followed by several questions. Read the requirements and constraints once, then answer every question against them. Microsoft's break rules differ inside case-study and problem/solution sets.

sections.title: 1.1 Define and configure foundational Customer Service components
sections.html:
Skills measured: implement and monitor record creation and update rules • configure and modify the case resolution experience • configure and manage security roles • configure the timeline control, including records, card forms, and highlights. Build an email-to-case rule and read its activity monitor, change the Resolve case dialog, map a copied role to a persona, and add a timeline with a custom card form. Admin screens are in the Copilot Service admin center (older pages call it the Customer Service admin center).

Implement and monitor record creation and update rules

Modern automatic record creation (ARC) rules create or update records from activities: email, social activity, task, phone call, appointment, service activity or a custom activity. A rule holds rule items (a condition plus an action). Every active rule item runs as a Power Automate cloud flow named ARC: <rule item name>, so a rule with no rule item has no flow and does nothing. Modern rules are not supported on-premises.

  1. Customer support > Case settings > Automatic record creation and update rules > Manage > New.
  2. Basic tab, Step one: details: Rule name, Queue scope (Track multiple queues or Track single queue), Queue to monitor (an email rule cannot be activated without a queue) and Activity type to monitor = Email. Save enables step two.
  3. Step two: conditions to evaluate and actions to take: New opens the Condition builder. Add at least one condition, confirm Actions to take > Record to create = Case, select Save and open in Power Automate, then Save & Close.
  4. Step three: set Automatically reply to email; if Yes, choose an email template.
  5. Optionally tune the Advanced tab, then activate the rule. It stays Draft until you do.
Advanced tab setting (Before evaluating conditions)What it does
Allow emails from unknown sendersYes = a case is created even when the sender is not in any contact or account record.
Manage unknown senders byCreating a new contact automatically, or Mapping in Power Automate manually (you must then map the customer field in the flow).
Require a valid entitlement on the connected caseYes = a case is created only if an active entitlement exists for the customer. For a contact with a parent account, the account's entitlement must list the contact or have an empty Contacts section.
Wait for a specific amount of time after the connected case is resolvedYes + a time = no new case until that time has passed after the related case was resolved. Yes + no time = a new case immediately. No = no new case while a related case exists. The resolved case is not reopened automatically; a Power Automate flow must do that.
Owner whose permissions the rule uses to runDefaults to the user who created the rule.
  • Rule items are evaluated top-down. The first match creates the case and the remaining items are skipped, so reorder items to change priority.
  • A queue cannot be in both a single-queue and a multiple-queue rule (deactivate the old rule first), and a single-queue rule cannot be converted into a multiple-queue rule or the reverse: create a new rule.
  • One email reaching the Sales, Support and Billing mailboxes creates duplicate cases. Route them to one dedicated queue with one rule. For the opposite goal, one case per queue-enabled mailbox, set the Power Apps setting definition Email Multi Related for ARC to Yes (default No) and Publish All Customizations.
  • By default a contact for an unknown sender is created in the context of the email recipient. Set the environment variable msdyn_ArcCreateContactWithRuleOwner to 1 to create it as the rule owner.
  • Web-client ARC rules were deprecated on October 1, 2020. Migrate them in Operations > Miscellaneous > ARC and SLA migration > Manage; the migration does not change the old rules.

Activity monitor (online environments only) shows how each activity was evaluated. It tracks a rule only until the rule has been evaluated in Customer Service, which is before the Power Automate flow runs. Open it from the Activity monitor events (past 7 days) tile on the Customer support overview, or from Case settings > ARC rules > View activity monitor. Columns: Current state, Rule name, Monitored activity type (hidden in the 7-day view; add it with Edit columns), Monitored activity item, Condition name, Reason, Recommendation and Evaluated on. Monitor options filters the states. To reprocess activities, open All Activities, select them and use Add To Queue.

Current stateMeaningTypical fix
FailedAn error occurred during evaluation.Read the Reason and Recommendation, fix, then reprocess.
SkippedSkipped by design: a setting or condition was not met.Unknown sender: Allow emails from unknown senders = Yes. Connected case already resolved: Wait ... = Yes. No entitlement: Require a valid entitlement = No.
Ready for Power AutomateThe rule passed evaluation; the flow takes over.No case appeared: check the flow run history. If the rule lost its flow connection, deactivate and reactivate it.
Exam traps
  • Skipped is not an error. Only Failed is. Skipped tells you which setting stopped the email.
  • The monitor stops before the flow. "Ready for Power Automate" with no case means checking the flow run, not the rule conditions.
  • Queue scope and Queue to monitor are different fields, and a rule's scope cannot be changed after the fact.
  • The wait-after-resolution setting allows or delays a new case. It never reopens the resolved case.

Configure and modify the case resolution experience

Resolve case dialog optionUse it when
Standard dialog (default)The out-of-box dialog (Resolution Type and Resolution). Setting Enable minimal case resolution dialog to No brings back the older dialog and only works while this option is selected.
Customizable dialogYou must add or remove fields or add resolution values by editing the Case Resolution table form in Power Apps.
Quick create dialogThird option. Like Customizable dialog, it is customized with the Modify the case resolution dialog steps (for example to add Duration, Billable Time or Total Time).

Path: Customer support > Case settings > Other settings > Manage > Service Configuration Settings > Resolve case dialog. Two further levers are Power Apps setting definitions:

Setting definitionEffect and how to set it
Redirect user to the specified tab to close open activitiesChooses the tab opened by the link on the "open activities" warning. In the form designer select the tab and copy its Name from Display options (not the label). Paste it into the environment value, or into Setting app values > New app value to override the environment value for one app. Then Publish All Customizations.
Enable minimal case resolution dialogNo = legacy dialog (adds duration and billable time). Requires Resolve case dialog = Standard dialog.
  1. Add Billable Time: set Resolve case dialog to Customizable dialog and Save. In Power Apps open Tables > Case Resolution > Forms, add Billable Time (add Total Time too so it fills automatically), then Save and publish.
  2. Add a resolution type: in Tables > Case > Columns > Status Reason add a choice under the Resolved status (for example Duplicate) and copy its Value. In Tables > Case Resolution > Columns > Resolution Type add the same label and the same Value. Save and publish both. A mismatch can cause an error or the value is not displayed.
  • Case resolution is not supported if the Regarding column is added to the dialog.
  • Privileges on Environment Variable Definition: CSR Manager needs Create, Read and Write; Customer Service Representative needs Read. Custom roles must be updated to use a modified dialog.
  • Case update after resolution (Other settings): Allow updates for = Resolved and canceled cases (default), Resolved cases, Closed cases or Don't allow updates. Updates come from Power Automate flows or an API (for example GDPR clean-up); the case does not need reopening.
  • The rep-side "Propose new knowledge article for this case" checkbox on this dialog belongs to a Preview feature (see §1.2).
Exam traps
  • Paste the tab Name, not its label, and remember an app value overrides the environment value.
  • The minimal-dialog setting restores the legacy dialog; it does not make the dialog customizable.
  • Add the resolution value to both the Case Status Reason and the Case Resolution Resolution Type columns.
  • Case-update-after-resolution does not unlock the form for reps; it enables flow or API updates.

Configure and manage security roles

  • A user can hold many roles and privileges are cumulative (the broadest grant wins). Roles belong to a business unit, and every user needs at least one role, directly or through a group team.
  • Privilege types: Tables (Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append To, Assign, Share), Miscellaneous (task privileges such as publishing articles) and Privacy-related.
Access level (UI)SDK / privilege-table nameRecords the user can reach
OrganizationGlobalAll records in the organization
Parent: Child Business UnitDeepOwn business unit and every subordinate unit
Business UnitLocalRecords in the user's business unit
UserBasicRecords they own or that are shared with them or their teams
NoneNoneNo access

For organization-owned tables, and for miscellaneous and privacy privileges, only Organization or None is available.

  1. Create: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > your environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > + New role. Defaults: Member's privilege inheritance = Direct User (Basic) access level and Team privileges; Include App Opener privileges = On.
  2. Customise by copy: select a role > Copy security role > name it > Copy > edit privileges > save. The System Administrator role cannot be edited and the settings (name, description) of system roles are locked, so copy the nearest role. App Opener is the minimum role to run a model-driven app.
  3. Assign: Users > select the user > Manage security roles. The assigner needs at least Read and Assign on the Security Role table and cannot grant a role with more privileges than they hold; a CSR Manager cannot assign System Administrator.
RolePurpose
Customer Service RepresentativeRequired to work with cases; the only role with Copilot features by default.
CSR ManagerManager role for queues, ARC rules and similar tasks.
Basic UserRequired by all Contact Center users.
Omnichannel administrator / supervisor / agentContact Center admin, supervisor and representative tasks. The administrator also needs System Administrator to manage roles.
App Profile Manager Administrator / App Profile UserCreate and assign app profiles / use them.
Productivity tools user / administratorUse / administer productivity tools. Multisession Teams chat needs the same permissions as the user role.

Persona mapping (unified routing): copy one of Omnichannel Administrator, Omnichannel supervisor, Omnichannel agent, CSR Manager or Customer Service Representative, keep the persona privilege (prvAdmin, prvSupervisor or prvAgent), then go to Customer support > User management > Role persona mapping > Manage > select the persona > Edit roles > Save and Close. It needs the System Administrator role. With Customer Service Enterprise the defaults are Admin = CSR Manager, Supervisor = CSR Manager, Agent = Customer Service Representative. Mapped roles must be assigned to users directly, not through team membership, and mapping does not grant app or form access: also assign the app (Manage roles on the app tile) and enable the roles on forms.

  • Other Customer Service privileges: custom roles need the Copilot table privileges plus the miscellaneous prvIntelligenceUsage; disconnecting Teams chats uses Business management > Miscellaneous privileges > Disconnect Teams chat from Dynamics 365 record (§1.3). Do not give the Omnichannel API access role to supervisors or reps.
  • Entra security-group teams give the whole group the same roles; assign Basic User, Customer Service Representative and Omnichannel agent to the team.
Exam traps
  • Persona mapping silently fails when roles arrive through a team. Assign directly.
  • Do not edit a system role: copy it. Start a new representative role from the closest predefined role to avoid under-granting.
  • User level (Basic) is not the Basic User role; the first is an access level, the second a role.
  • Mapping a role to a persona does not open apps, dashboards or forms for the user.

Configure the timeline control, including records, card forms, and highlights

  1. Power Apps > Tables > your table > Forms > the form > Components > drag Timeline onto a section. Save and Publish; changes are invisible until you do. A form can host several timelines.
  2. Display options: Records shown on page defaults to 10 (up to 50); Load more appears after that. Record types to show are Activities, Notes and Posts (all on by default; posts need a Dynamics 365 app).
  3. Advanced: Quick entry record type (Notes or Posts; default Notes), filter pane, search bar, expand-all and the "What you've missed" summary.
  4. Record settings per activity type: enable or disable the type, pick its card form, show Regarding records (linked through rollup), and choose how activities are sorted (Last Updated, or a Sort date column that you populate yourself with Power Automate, a business rule or JavaScript).
  • A custom table appears on a timeline only if its table Type is Activity. Command actions on activity types (assign, close, delete, open, add to queue; at most five) are Preview.
  • Activity rollup for account and contact timelines: Extended, Related or None (None shows only activities directly related to the table).
  • Performance and limits: more than 10 selected activity types shows a warning; a timeline can link at most 15 tables (error 0x8004430d, "Number of link entity ... exceed limit 15"); the timeline does not refresh automatically when post replies are added.
  • Link a note to another record: notes can be linked to an account, contact or case only, using Link to Table in the Notes menu; the note moves to the target record.
Card form sectionColumns allowedShown on the timeline record
ColorStrip-Never; it is the strip on the left of the card
HeaderUp to 6Only the first 2 (title/subject and, for example, Modified On)
DetailsUp to 4Only the first 3
Footer-Never

Each activity type needs its own card form. A new card form (type Card) must be added on the parent table before it appears in the timeline's list of card forms; "Default" means no card form is in use, and an email card form is used only after you select it and publish the form. Empty columns are ignored.

Timeline highlights use Copilot to list the significant activities on a record (from notes, emails, tasks, appointments, phone calls and conversations), follow the current timeline filters and have a Copy button. Turn them on at app level (Power Apps > Apps > the app > Settings > Upcoming > Enable Timeline Highlights) or at form level (Enable Timeline Highlights powered by Generative AI). Copilot must be on in the app's settings and the environment must have Enable Dynamics 365 apps set. The modern Timeline control is a separate Upcoming toggle ("Enable a modern Timeline control experience").

Exam traps
  • Header shows only 2 columns and Details only 3, even when you place more; Footer and ColorStrip never show.
  • Card forms are per activity type, and a new card form must be added to the parent table first.
  • Highlights are not enabled by the card form or filter settings; they come from the Upcoming app setting or the form-level option plus Copilot.
  • Notes link only to account, contact or case; the 15-table limit is the usual reason a timeline fails to load.
