sections.title: 1.2 Create and administer knowledge management
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure internal knowledge search capabilities • configure tables for knowledge management • manage translated knowledge articles • integrate and search external knowledge sources • configure AI suggestions and Copilot-led knowledge article creation. Build: switch on search mode "all", add a custom record type, create and publish a translation, ingest a public site with an integrated provider, and enable the Customer Knowledge Management Agent. Admin screens: Copilot Service admin center > Support experience > Knowledge.

Configure internal knowledge search capabilities

You need the System Administrator or System Customizer role (or equivalent) and must be the Microsoft 365 tenant administrator. The KnowledgeArticle table's security boundary is the environment, not the individual user, so restrict access through table privileges. The search settings are in Knowledge > General settings > Manage.

Setting (Knowledge search experience)Behaviour
Set search mode as allEvery keyword must match. The default is searchMode=any, where any keyword matches, so "Contoso Coffee" returns articles with either word. Needs Dataverse search.
Enable suggest as you typeWhile reps type, the text is matched against article titles and the hits appear in a flyout with the matching text highlighted.
Show recently viewed knowledge articlesShows recent articles for a case; choose 1 to 8 to display.
Search results display countOnly for the app side pane control and the standalone knowledge search control.
Enable feedbackLets reps rate articles and give feedback.
Enable Kb preview mode from global search optionReps can preview articles that they find through global search.
  • Dataverse search is on by default in production environments, except those that use their own encryption key. Knowledge search uses it when enabled. If it is off, search switches to full-text search (SQL full-text queries).
  • What a result card shows (keywords, description, attachments, article number) depends on the Quick Find view columns of the Knowledge Article table.
  • Filters (Knowledge > Filters > Manage): set Enable search filters to Yes; Allow agent to personalize lets reps save the filters they use.
OperatorSyntaxExample
AND+Delivery + order
OR|delivery | order
NOT- before the keywordproduct -order
Wildcard* at the start or end of a keywordpro* finds product, procedure
Exact phrasedouble quotation marks (common words such as a, an, the are ignored)"order shipping time"
App typeSearch controlWhere you configure it
Multisession apps (Copilot Service workspace)Knowledge search control on the app side paneAdmin center > Knowledge > Record types > Edit
Single-session apps, or automatic search on non-anchor tabsKnowledge Base Search form controlPower Apps > Tables > table > Forms > section > + Component > Related Data > Knowledge Search

The form control is already on the Case main form (Activity wall section) and the Case for interactive experience form (Related section). Its Results shown on page value is ignored once at least one external search provider exists (each provider then shows three articles).

Exam traps
  • Set search mode as all only changes the matching logic and relies on Dataverse search; without it search falls back to full-text. It is not the same as suggest-as-you-type.
  • Suggest-as-you-type matches article titles, not the full content.
  • The Knowledge Search form control is for single-session apps. Copilot Service workspace uses the side pane control configured in the admin center.
  • Operators are symbols: + AND, | OR, - NOT, * wildcard, quotes for an exact phrase.

Configure tables for knowledge management

  • The KnowledgeArticle table replaced the legacy KbArticle, KbArticleComment and KbArticleTemplate tables Removed. Creating an article also creates a root article that holds every version and translation. The article starts in Draft with major version 1 and minor version 0, and ArticlePublicNumber stays the same across versions and translations.
  • statecode values: 0 Draft, 1 Approved, 2 Scheduled, 3 Published, 4 Expired, 5 Archived, 6 Discarded. This is the lifecycle, not confidentiality.
  • Duplicate detection rules are not supported on the Knowledge Article table.
  1. Knowledge > Record types > Manage > Add > choose the record type > Save and Close.
  2. Select the record type > Edit to open Knowledge settings: Automatic search (turn it on and choose Provide search results using a field), Actions (Link / unlink article, Copy URL, Link article and email URL, Link article and send article content) and Email recipient (only for Customer or Lookup attributes that point to an account or contact).
  • Case and Conversation are enabled by default (Conversation when a chat, digital messaging or voice add-on is licensed). Any other table, including a custom one, has to be added. The side pane settings are available only in the Copilot Service admin center.
  • Articles are linked to other tables through a many-to-many relationship named msdyn_<table>_knowledgearticle (for example msdyn_account_knowledgearticle); for cases the intersect table is KnowledgeArticleIncident.
  • Categories (Knowledge > Categories > Manage > New): Title, Description, Display Order, Parent Category and a Category Number shown after the first save. Roles: Customer Service Manager, System Administrator or System Customizer. The Categories lookup view is not customizable.
  • Publishing needs Publish and Update on the Knowledge Article table (default for Knowledge Manager, Customer Service Manager, Customer Service Representative and System Administrator). Changing a Published article needs the Publish privilege.
Exam traps
  • Only Case and Conversation are on by default; a custom table must be added as a record type.
  • Do not use the retired KbArticle tables: the answer is always KnowledgeArticle.
  • Versions and translations are separate article records under one root and share the same article number.
  • A Draft article is not hidden: users with Read and Write can open it. State is the lifecycle stage.

Manage translated knowledge articles

  1. In Copilot Service workspace open Knowledge Articles > the article > Translate on the command bar.
  2. In Create new translation, choose Pick a Language (the languages your instance supports) and Create new version = Major or Minor, then Create.
  3. Enter the translated Title, Keywords, Article Description and Content.
  4. Review and approve, then More > Publish.
Publish dialog fieldMeaning
Publish / Publish OnPublish now or schedule a date and time.
Published StatusStatus after publishing (default Published).
Expiration Date / Expiration StatusExpired articles no longer appear in searches; the status field sets what they become.
Publish Approved related translations with ArticleYes = approved translations go live together with the source article.
  • Manage translations on the Summary tab > Related Information > Related Translations: edit, create a new major or minor version, or delete. A language can have several versions.
  • The Publish dialog appears only for the default business process flow whose last stage is Publish. Only users with the Publish privilege can update a Published or Scheduled article.
  • Developers: CreateKnowledgeArticleTranslation copies title, content, description and keywords into a new record for the requested LanguageLocale (more than 150 languages) and links it to the primary article through ParentArticleContentId. Versions use RootArticleId.
  • Authoring language (General settings): set Enable default authoring language to Yes, pick Organization's UI language or Other language plus a language, and optionally Allow users to set default knowledge authoring language.
Exam traps
  • A translation adds a language; a new major or minor version updates content in the same language. Do not create a second article for another language.
  • Translations publish with the source only when you answer Yes to the related-translations option, and only approved ones are published.
  • The Translate command is on the article's command bar; managing existing translations is on the Summary tab.

Integrate and search external knowledge sources

External search providers (federated)Integrated search providers
Admin tileKnowledge > External search providers (renamed from Search Providers)Knowledge > Integrated search providers
How it worksSearches the source live; reps see links per providerIngests third-party articles into Dataverse on a schedule, so they can be searched and filtered
TypesCross-Organizational Search, SharePoint, Microsoft Graph connector (unique connection ID)Third-party sources such as websites that follow the site map protocol
  • External: Manage > New > General (name, owner) > Details (organization and Search Type) > Save. Reps see three articles per provider plus Show more. Custom roles need Read, Create, Append and AppendTo on Knowledge Federated Article and Knowledge Federated Article Incident. In Microsoft Cloud for Sovereignty it is available in GCC only.
  • Integrated prerequisites: prvReadconnector (Basic) and Global prvReadWorkflow, prvWriteWorkflow and create/read/write/delete on msdyn_knowledgeconfiguration. First use: Integrated search providers > Manage > Set up integrated search; if that fails, turn on the Integrated Search API trigger flow (Power Apps > Solutions > Default Solution > Cloud flows).
  1. New > Provider info (name, description, authorization check box).
  2. Authentication and testing: Root URL, Site map URL (the site's /robots.txt shows it) and a language filter. The site map needs a lastmod tag in each url, content type application/xml or text/xml, and a static site; root URL, site map URL and language filter must be a unique combination.
  3. Knowledge article schema: Field Mapping or JSON Schema. The choice cannot be changed after saving.
  4. Refresh Schedule: frequency, lookback period; No refresh pauses ingestion.
  5. Summary > Save and close gives Inactive / Validated (Save as draft gives Inactive / Draft, which cannot ingest).
  6. Run a Trial ingestion (up to 1,000 records) and check Insights, Activate (Active / Ingestion Ready), then run time-range ingestion (limited to 60 days from the From date).

Field Mapping needs a sample page saved as Web Page, HTML Only. The mandatory attributes are Content, External Reference Id (must be unique) and Title; operation types are Regex (needs a capture group), Direct, Constant and RegexUrl. A JSON schema starts like this, and DocFieldSource accepts Regex, Meta, Constant, Url or Document:

{
  "Name": "Contoso help site",
  "UniqueTargetFieldName": "msdyn_externalreferenceid",
  "ContentTargetFieldName": "content",
  "ApiPathLeafName": "knowledgearticles",
  "FieldDefinitions": [
    { "DocFieldSource": "Regex", "DocFieldPattern": "<title>(.*?)</title>",
      "TargetFieldName": "title", "TargetFieldType": "String" },
    { "DocFieldSource": "Document", "TargetFieldName": "content", "TargetFieldType": "String" }
  ]
}

A real template must also carry the default definitions for articlepublicnumber, msdyn_isingestedarticle, msdyn_ingestedarticleurl and msdyn_integratedsearchproviderid@odata.bind. UniqueTargetFieldName is the out-of-the-box msdyn_externalreferenceid (or a custom column that is an alternate key); the content and API path values are fixed.

Exam traps
  • Federated (SharePoint, Graph connector, cross-organization) versus ingested (integrated): only integrated providers copy articles into Dataverse, and only they come from a site map.
  • A Draft provider cannot ingest, and the schema method (Field Mapping or JSON) cannot be changed after you save.
  • If a provider will not provision, turn on the Integrated Search API trigger flow before opening a support case.
  • Reps see three articles per provider (plus Show more) and the configured results count is ignored as soon as one external provider exists.

Configure AI suggestions and Copilot-led knowledge article creation

FeatureStatusWhat it does
Copilot knowledge drafts from cases (rep-driven)PreviewRep ticks Propose new knowledge article for this case on the Resolve Case dialog (or uses Propose Knowledge Article on a resolved case) and Copilot drafts an article.
Customer Knowledge Management AgentGA (some parts Preview)Autonomously turns cases, conversations, emails and notes into articles, in real time or from history.
Smart-assist AI suggestions of similar cases and articlesDeprecatedNo longer supported since June 2, 2025; Microsoft points to Copilot.
AI-suggested article keywords and descriptionsDeprecatedDeprecated December 15, 2025 (support ended January 31, 2026); use Fill forms using Copilot.

Rep-driven drafts. Prerequisites: System Administrator and knowledge management configured. In Knowledge > Knowledge creation (preview) > Manage, tick Let representatives use Copilot to propose new knowledge based on case information during or after case resolution and, optionally, In the case resolution step, keep the option to propose a knowledge article selected by default. In the draft the rep picks a template and language and selects Generate draft (default template: title, issue, cause, resolution), can use Revise with instructions up to five times, and ends with Create proposal.

Customer Knowledge Management Agent (Knowledge > Customer Knowledge Management Agent > Manage):

  • Prerequisites: out-of-the-box or custom case/conversation entity, knowledge management configured, Copilot allowed to use the Dynamics 365 knowledge base, pay-as-you-go billing set up, then in the page's Prerequisites section: Step 1 Connection References (Setup connections), Step 2 Power Automate Flows (Enable), Step 3 Copilot Studio Agent (Publish).
  • Real-time creation runs when a rep resolves a case or closes a conversation: the agent compares it with existing articles and creates one only if needed. Rules filter which items qualify; attribute mapping allows up to 10 one-to-one and 6 one-to-many attributes (Title and Description cannot be removed).
  • Historical creation processes up to 100,000 cases or conversations, is long-running and cannot be stopped once started, so run it in batches. A custom article template (one per rule) overrides the default Issue / Cause / Resolution format. Custom record types (up to five) and Automatically update existing articles (a new minor version by default) are Preview.
  • Compliance: set the default state (for example Pending so reviewers mark articles compliant). Noncompliant articles cannot be published. Auto publishing publishes compliant articles immediately to internal audiences or to internal and external audiences.
  • Without auto publishing, reps review drafts on the resolved case timeline (Suggested actions). This needs in-app notifications, permission to edit articles, and Timeline plus Timeline highlights enabled (§1.1).
  • Copilot features need Enable AI-powered Copilot features for the environment (Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings), and custom roles need Copilot privileges (§1.1).
Exam traps
  • Two different Copilot knowledge features: rep-driven drafts (Preview, one case at a time) versus the autonomous Customer Knowledge Management Agent (bulk and real time, can auto publish).
  • Smart-assist "AI suggestions" are deprecated; do not pick them for a new design.
  • Noncompliant articles cannot be published, so auto publishing only handles articles whose compliance status qualifies.
  • The agent needs consumption (pay-as-you-go) billing and connection references before it can run.

Sources: Configure knowledge management · Knowledge search operators · Side pane search control · Knowledge Base Search control · KnowledgeArticle table · Categories · Publish articles · Translate articles · External search providers · Integrated search providers · Schema mapping · Metadata schema · Knowledge from cases (preview) · Customer Knowledge Management Agent · Deprecations

sections.title: 1.3 Manage collaboration
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure Microsoft Teams chat • configure Join a Teams call for specific users • configure suggested contacts in Microsoft Teams, including by using AI and rules-based suggestions • configure Teams collaboration experience. Build: enable chat for a custom app, connect chats to a custom record type, turn on Join a Teams call for a custom experience profile, and create a rules-based suggestion rule with a custom action. All three features live under Copilot Service admin center > Support experience > Collaboration.

Configure Microsoft Teams chat

  1. Support experience > Collaboration > Embedded chat using Teams > Manage.
  2. Turn on Turn on Microsoft Teams chats inside Dynamics 365, then choose Turn on for all Dynamics 365 apps (also covers apps added later) or Turn on for selected Dynamics 365 apps. Save.
  3. Under Connect chats to Dynamics 365 records, pick a record type and set its options, or Add record types.
  • Teams chat is already on for Copilot Service workspace and Customer Service Hub. A custom app must be selected under "selected apps". It also works in other customer engagement apps such as Field Service and Sales. To open the settings page from a custom app, add a site map subarea of type URL with /main.aspx?pagetype=control&controlName=MscrmControls.TeamsCollaborationAdmin.TeamsCollaborationAdmin.
  • Specific multisession users: create a custom experience profile, then Embedded chat using Teams > Turn on for specific multisession users > Manage > open the profile (add users, session template, inbox, productivity pane features, channel providers). Multisession users need the same permissions as the Productivity tools user role.
  • Only the mapping between the record ID and the chat ID is stored in Dynamics 365 (the Preview chat sync below adds timeline data). Guest users and cross-tenant access may not work. Chats are connected only as group chats; a one-to-one chat cannot be connected.
Graph permissionUsed for
Chat.ReadWrite.AllReading chats and recent messages for the chat list
Directory.Read.AllDisplay names of the user's teams and channels
Presence.Read.AllPresence shown on avatars
User.Read.AllDisplay name and licenses, to check that suggested participants have a Teams license
User.ReadBasic.AllUsers' photos
Per record type (Connect chats to Dynamics 365 records)Behaviour
Include a noteContext card built from a view; the first five fields are used and unsupported field types are skipped. The data is static, so field-level security is not checked for collaborators. Defaults: Case introduction message view for Case, Quick find view for other standard types.
Join chatLets users with write access to the record view and join chats that are connected to it, even if they were not in the chat (case transfers and escalations). On by default for Case. Works only for connected chats.
Record owner can disconnect chats / Chat connector can disconnect chatOn by default for new organizations. At role level, grant the miscellaneous privilege Disconnect Teams chat from Dynamics 365 record (Business management > Miscellaneous privileges).
Receive notification on key updatesPosts a message to the chat when up to five selected attributes change. Case is preconfigured with Priority, Status and Status Reason. Not supported: virtual tables, tables without an Update message filter, and PartyList, Image, Integer and File attributes.

Sync Teams chats with records Preview shows connected chats as timeline activities. Only global administrators can enable it. Microsoft's pages do not say whether chats connected before it was turned on sync, so don't assume either way. Multisession users also need Teams integration turned on in the productivity pane of their app profile. Customer support swarming Deprecated (since February 8, 2026): use embedded Teams chat.

Exam traps
  • "Selected apps" is how a custom app gets chat. Join chat, suggested contacts and chat sync do not turn chat on.
  • Joining needs both the Join chat setting for that record type and write access; record ownership is not required, and read-only users cannot join.
  • One-to-one chats cannot be connected to a record.
  • Sync Teams chats with records is Preview and needs a global administrator; without it, Dynamics 365 stores only the record-to-chat mapping.

Configure Join a Teams call for specific users

Join a Teams call lets a representative share their screen, use video and offer remote control to a customer. Customers do not need a Teams license or prior Teams experience. The feature is on by default in Copilot Service workspace for agent profiles that have Dynamics 365 Contact Center enabled.

PrerequisiteDetail
Collaboration settingPower Platform admin center > Settings > Product > Collaboration: turn on the setting that lets end users join Teams meetings (the Join a Teams call article calls it End users can join Teams meetings from appointments).
Teams accessRepresentatives must be able to access and use Teams.
Productivity paneRepresentatives must be able to open the productivity pane to see the Join a Teams call app.
Outbound emailOnly needed when representatives email the invitation; their email must be configured for outbound mail.
  1. Support experience > Collaboration > Join a Teams call > Manage.
  2. Turn on Join a Teams call. (Skip this step if it was never turned off.)
  3. For custom agent profiles that are not on by default, select Manage next to Turn on for specific multisession users and enable the feature for those profiles.
  4. Save.
Exam traps
  • A missing icon for reps on a custom profile is fixed per profile (Turn on for specific multisession users), not by a role or license change.
  • Outbound email is required only for emailing the invitation, not for the feature itself.
  • Join a Teams call (customer-facing screen share and video) is not Teams chat and not Meeting integration using Teams, which is a separate Preview feature.

Configure suggested contacts in Microsoft Teams, including by using AI and rules-based suggestions

Suggested contacts appear when a representative starts a new connected chat. Both types are switched on per record type (Collaboration > Embedded chat using Teams > Manage > Connect chats to Dynamics 365 records > record type > Suggest contacts).

AI-based suggested contactsRules-based suggested contacts
Record typesCase or ConversationAny record type enabled for connected chats (for Case you can use both types)
ToggleAI-based suggested contactsRules-based suggested contacts
How it worksFinds similar cases, then ranks the people who resolved them by number of similar cases resolved, similarity, recency and average resolution time. Out-of-box models; no training. The first use needs about 24 hours of preprocessing.Evaluates the rules you define, in the order you choose. Maximum 10 rules per record type.
PrerequisitesThe article lists AI suggestions for similar cases enabled, plus tenant permission for the enhanced Teams integration. The smart-assist version of AI suggestions is Deprecated (§1.2), so confirm the current requirement in the tenant.None beyond Teams chat. For localized rule names, users need Read on msdyn_contactsuggestionrule and msdyn_contactsuggestionruleset.
  1. Turn on Rules-based suggested contacts for the record type.
  2. Under Update rules for suggesting contacts, select Add new rule, enter a Rule name and choose the Rule type: Relational (a user on the record or on up to 10 chained related tables) or Custom (a custom action that you wrote). Save.
  3. Reorder, disable or delete rules with the hover controls. Users see suggestions in the order you set; disabling keeps the rule, deleting removes it.

A Custom rule calls an existing custom action, passes it the record id and table, and expects users back. The action must have these arguments:

NameTypeRequiredDirection
EntityLogicalNameStringRequiredInput
RecordidStringRequiredInput
CustomActionSuggestedUsersStringRequiredOutput
CustomActionInputsStringOptionalInput

The output is a list of objects with AADUserId (Guid), systemUserId (Guid) and description (string). Two optional toggles on the AI page are Turn on Enhanced Microsoft Teams Integration and Enable Confidential Labels (see below).

Exam traps
  • AI-based suggestions exist only for Case and Conversation; every other record type is rules-based.
  • Ten rules is a hard maximum per record type, and rule order is display order, not alphabetical.
  • The custom action needs exactly these argument names and directions; the output is a list of users, not a single user id.
  • Deleting a rule removes it permanently; disabling only stops it from contributing suggestions.

Configure Teams collaboration experience

Collaboration tileWhat it configuresStatus
Embedded chat using TeamsChat, connected record types, join and disconnect rules, suggested contacts, key-update notificationsGA (chat sync is Preview)
Join a Teams callScreen share, video and remote control with customersGA
Meeting integration using Teams (preview)Dynamics 365 record side panel in Teams meetingsPreview
  • Collaboration features are available in the Copilot Service admin center, Customer Service Hub, Copilot Service workspace and custom apps. Customer support swarming also appears in older overview pages but is Deprecated.
  • Turn on Enhanced Microsoft Teams Integration lets representatives pin records and views to a Teams channel directly from Dynamics 365 and also suggests representatives who worked on similar cases. Enable Confidential Labels lets them create private Teams messages and add sensitivity or confidentiality labels. The suggested-contact articles name the page toggle Turn on the linking of Dynamics 365 records to Microsoft Teams channels, while the chat article uses Turn on Microsoft Teams chats inside Dynamics 365; know both labels.
  • Meeting integration prerequisites: a Customer Service license, the Power Platform admin center setting that lets representatives add and join Teams meetings (required), and optionally Sync calendars (server-side synchronization). Enable it with Collaboration > Meeting integration using Teams (preview) > Manage > Show Dynamics 365 data in Teams meetings (preview) = Yes > Save. Do not use it in production; Microsoft does not provide support for this preview feature.
  • The record side panel supports only Contact, Opportunity, Lead, Account and Case. Customise it through the table's In Context Form (Power Apps > Dataverse > Tables > Forms): you can add or remove header fields and Key Details fields, change a field label and set a field read-only. You cannot enable, disable or rearrange tabs, add custom tabs or sections, add a web resource or subgrid, or change layout.
  • For meetings to show on the Outlook and Teams calendar, enable server-side synchronization for appointments, contacts and tasks on the mailbox, then Approve email and Test & Enable mailbox.
Exam traps
  • Meeting integration is Preview and not for production; Join a Teams call and embedded chat are GA.
  • Pinning records and views to a Teams channel comes from Enhanced Microsoft Teams Integration, not from Join chat or the meeting side panel.
  • The side panel supports five tables only and tabs cannot be added or reordered.
  • Swarming appears in some overview pages but is deprecated; embedded Teams chat replaces it.

Sources: Configure Teams chat · Teams chat FAQ · Use Teams chat · Set up Join a Teams call · Rules-based suggested contacts · AI-suggested contacts · Teams meetings (preview) · Collaboration overview · Deprecations

sections.title: 1.4 Manage agents and Copilot in Service features
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure Ask a Question, including filtering content • Configure case, timeline, and conversation summaries • Configure Draft a Response • Configure the Case Management Agent • Integrate agents with Customer Service, including plug-ins and knowledge sources. Practise by enabling Copilot in a trial environment and building one filter of each kind.

Configure Ask a Question, including filtering content

Ask a question is the chat tab of the Copilot help pane; Copilot answers from the configured knowledge sources and cites them. Two admin centers are involved, so order matters.

StepWhereWhat to know
1. Environment switchPower Platform admin center: Copilot > Settings > Copilot (under Dynamics 365 Customer Service) > select the environment > Edit setting > Enable AI-powered Copilot featuresRequired for Customer Service Hub and custom apps. In-region by default for US, Australia, India, UK, GCC and GCC High; Europe has data movement on by default; elsewhere allow it first.
2. Opt inCopilot Service admin center: Support experience > Productivity > Copilot settings (or Operations > Insights > Summaries) > Opt inReview data movement and the terms first. Opting out erases training data.
3. Make it availableWorkspace: experience profiles (the defaults already include Copilot). Hub: every rep once the feature is on. Custom apps: setting Customer Service Copilot Enabled = Yes.Reps need the Customer Service Representative role, or a custom role with the Copilot table privileges plus prvIntelligenceUsage. Configuring needs System Administrator. Experience profiles: §2.3.
4. Pick experiencesProductivity > Copilot settings > ManageCopilot help pane - Ask a Question and Copilot immersive Preview (Copilot Hub; production-ready). Both must also be on in the experience profile.
5. Configure the agentAgents within Copilot > Customer Support (button labelled Manage or Settings, depending on the page)Tabs: Overview, Immersive settings, Email settings, Prompts, Extend agent.

Customer Support agent: Overview tab

  • Instructions: up to 5,000 characters of guidance on tone, formatting, escalation, compliance reminders and terminology. They are applied only when your organization's Dynamics 365 knowledge base is the selected source; they are not applied to Copilot Studio sources.
  • Deterministic response (repeatable output for the same input), Enhanced features, Suggested prompts and Proactive insights.
  • Knowledge sources are off by default. Tick Include a knowledge base or another type of knowledge source, then Use your organization's knowledge base as knowledge source. Copilot reads only the content attribute, only Published latest-version articles, and only articles in the same language as the user interface. Knowledge setup is in §1.2.
FeatureDynamics 365 knowledge baseExternal web resources (trusted webpages)Copilot Studio knowledge sources
Ask a questionYesNoYes
Write an emailYesYesNo

Filters

Open Manage Filters to restrict which knowledge articles Copilot may use. Filters apply to Ask a question and to the draft features, are available in Dynamics 365 Customer Service only, and allow up to five filters per category. Filter fields must be String, Whole Number, Option Set or Two Options; other types such as Lookup are not supported.

TypeReps can see it?How you set it up
PresetNo. Runs in the background.Manage rules under Preset filters > conditions > Finish editing.
RepresentativeYes. Reps choose it under Filters > Select filters > Apply in the Copilot pane.+ Add Filter > knowledge field, display name and selectable values > turn on Filter status (without it reps never see the filter) > Finish editing.
AutomatedApplied automatically from the record type and values of the record the rep has open.+ Add Filter > field and rules > optional Use untagged content if the field value is null > Allow representatives to view or change this filter. On: you are prompted to create the matching representative filter and reps see a visual cue. Off: hidden, no notification.

When automated and representative filters both apply, Copilot uses both.

Verbatim answers

For approved wording (legal or regulatory text), mark the knowledge article, not the Copilot settings: add the keyword doNotSummarize to return a whole article verbatim, or use the Verbatim icon on a selected section. It affects Ask a question only. The Ask a question page labels the verbatim review experience (preview).

RequirementUse
Hidden scoping the rep must not changePreset filter
Let the rep choose a topic such as departmentRepresentative filter with Filter status on
Scope by the open record (case region); reps may overrideAutomated filter with Allow representatives to view or change this filter on
Answers from SharePoint, public sites or an external systemCopilot Studio knowledge or tools (see the integration topic below)
Exam traps
  • Preset filters are hidden, representative filters need the Filter status toggle, and automated filters follow the open record. They are not interchangeable.
  • Instructions do not apply to Copilot Studio sources, and trusted webpages never feed Ask a question; they feed emails and chat replies only.
  • Customer Service Hub and custom apps need the Power Platform admin center switch; experience profiles only control Copilot Service workspace.

Configure case, timeline, and conversation summaries

SummaryWhere reps see itAvailable in
Case summary (and custom record summaries)Card on the case form; also through Ask a questionCopilot Service workspace; Customer Service Hub and custom apps need the Power Platform admin center switch (custom apps also the Customer Service Copilot Enabled setting in Power Apps)
Conversation summaryConversation panel; Summary tab of a closed conversationCopilot Service workspace only
Timeline (documented as timeline highlights)Bulleted list at the top of the timelineApps and forms where you enable it

Case summaries

  1. In Copilot Service admin center turn on Ask a question (under Copilot for questions and emails).
  2. Go to Support Experience > Productivity > Summaries (or Operations > Insights > Summaries) and select Manage.
  3. Select Make case summaries available to representatives.
  4. Select Manage data to change the source fields.
  5. Select Specify information to exclude: up to 10 email addresses and three disclaimers, headers or footers.
  • A summary needs at least 50 tokens, about 38 English words, across the source fields, otherwise none is generated. Resolved and canceled cases can be summarized.
  • The wizard (Manage data, or Add new summary for custom records) has four panes: Specify record type (including verbosity Small, Medium or Large), Specify data, Include related record summary (optional) and Manage summary format.
  • Specify data: 1-to-1 data up to 10 selections; 1-to-many up to six selections across at most three related entities; at least one 1-to-1 row for case summaries. The defaults start with Customer, Case Title, Case Type, Subject, Case Description, Product and Priority (keep at least one of these seven enabled). Product needs the prvReadProduct privilege.
  • Related record summary: choose the related record, the field that references the parent and the summary configuration. Reps see two related summaries by default and load two more with Show more related records.
  • Format: Paragraph, or Structured with up to five headers (defaults Issue, Troubleshooting steps, Outcome, Error code, Root cause).
  • Custom case forms do not show the card automatically: add the web resource msdyn_CopilotCaseSummaryLibrary.js and the control mscrmcontrols.csintelligence.copilotcasesummarycontrol, bind Case Summary to an unused string column and Incident ID to Case (Text), and add the On load handler Mscrm.CSIntelligence.CopilotCaseSummary.setVisibilityOfCaseSummary so the card stays hidden when Copilot is off. Custom apps need Customer Service Copilot Enabled. A custom record summary also gives you a Developer summary ID.

Conversation summaries

Option on the Summaries pageWhen a summary is generated
When a representative joins a conversationWhen a rep joins; also when the primary rep invites a collaborator who joins, or transfers the conversation
When a conversation endsAt the end; optional Allow customer service representatives to create case with a button in the summary adds Create case; it also shows on the Summary tab of the closed conversation
On demandWhen a rep selects Summarize conversation

Use Manage format (Live conversation summaries) to choose Paragraph or Structured. Structured defaults are Root cause, Customer issue, Troubleshooting steps, Outcome, Error code; you can add, reorder and reset sections. AI agent conversations are not automatically included. Auto-summarization of ongoing conversations was deprecated on April 16, 2025.

Timeline highlights

Copilot builds a bulleted list from the most recent notes, emails, tasks, appointments, phone calls and conversations that match the timeline filters; it has no settings of its own. With Copilot turned on in the app settings, enable it for an app (Power Apps > Apps > the app > Settings > Upcoming > Enable Timeline Highlights > save and publish) or for one form (table > Forms > the form > Enable Timeline Highlights powered by Generative AI). The environment needs Enable Dynamics 365 apps on. The timeline control itself is in §1.1.

Exam traps
  • Case and conversation summaries have different default structured sections: case = Issue first; conversation = Root cause first and includes Customer issue.
  • Conversation summaries exist only in Copilot Service workspace; case summaries in Customer Service Hub and custom apps need the Power Platform admin center switch (custom apps also the Customer Service Copilot Enabled setting), and custom case forms need the case summary control built in Power Apps.
  • Below about 38 English words in the source fields, no case summary appears.
  • "On demand" is not an automatic trigger, and the Create case button is a sub-option of the end-of-conversation trigger.

Configure Draft a Response

Microsoft Learn currently has no standalone article named "Draft a response". What the docs document today, and its status:

CapabilityStatus in the docsConfiguration
Draft a chat responseDeprecated The Contact Center deprecations article says the feature (preview) was deprecated on July 1, 2025, with support removed on July 14, 2025. A few pages still use the name.Nothing to configure. Reps use Ask a question and Send to customer in an active digital messaging conversation.
Write an email (help pane) and Draft with Copilot (email editor)The setup pages carry no preview label, but the Manage Copilot features page says composing an email is generally available in North America only and in preview in the other supported regions. Email sentiments is a preview option.See below.
Case Management AgentDrafts customer emails during case resolution.See the Case Management Agent topic.
Service Agent in Microsoft 365 CopilotCan draft responses and emails after review (GA as a Microsoft 365 Copilot agent).See the integration topic.

Email drafting

  • Help pane: Copilot Service admin center > Productivity (or Operations > Insights) > Copilot for questions and emails > Manage > turn on Help pane - Write an email > Save.
  • Inline in the rich text editor: Power Apps > Apps > the app > Settings > Features > Contextual email drafting with AI = Yes. It works in version two of the rich text editor only, which shows a Draft with Copilot card.
  • Copilot for email templates lets Copilot choose a template; it works only when the editor is empty and shows five recommended templates.
  • Knowledge for drafting is off by default; enable it on the Customer Support agent. Trusted webpages (Email settings tab): up to five domains, searched two levels down, Bing Search must be enabled in the Power Platform admin center, and the Bing Search API they rely on is flagged as deprecated. They are used for emails and chat replies only.
Exam traps
  • Do not plan a configuration for "Draft a chat response (preview)": it is deprecated and removed.
  • Two switches enable email drafting: the help-pane toggle in Copilot Service admin center and the inline-editor toggle in Power Apps.
  • Copilot-recommended email templates are skipped when the editor already contains text.

Configure the Case Management Agent

Case Management Agent (CMA) automates the case lifecycle through three flows you configure independently or combine. Status: Learn labels shadow mode Preview in all three flows, and simulation preview for resolution and closure. The setup pages carry no other preview label, but the archived release plans give differing dates for autonomous email resolution, so treat that flow's exact GA status as unconfirmed.

FlowOperating modesKey points
Case creation and updateNo mode settingAutonomous creation from chat and voice; autonomous field updates when a conversation ends or an email arrives; AI-assisted creation from an email or conversation.
Case resolutionLevel of automation per line of business: Full, Require agent confirmation, Shadow mode, DisabledNeeds Customer Intent Agent. Full autonomy needs an application user and a shared mailbox.
Case follow-up and closureRequire human confirmation or Full automation per ruleRules with trigger, number of follow-ups, wait times and templates; the case is closed after the last unanswered follow-up.

Common setup

  1. Prerequisites: an Azure account with an active subscription, the Application Developer role and the CSR Manager or Customer Service Representative role.
  2. Power Platform admin center: Copilot > Settings > Agents > select the environment > Edit setting > Enable AI agents.
  3. Copilot Service admin center: Customer support > Case settings > Manage (Case Management Agent), complete the guided setup, then Manage the flow you need.
  4. CMA uses the Data Entry Agent and bills Copilot Credits; pay-as-you-go needs an Azure subscription.

Case creation and update

  • Prerequisites: AI form fill assistance enabled in the Power Platform admin center; automatic record creation and update rules (to create cases from email); channels, workstreams and queues (§2.1); authenticated chat (CMA creates and updates cases from authenticated chats only); data movement; transcription for voice; read on msdyn_entityattributepredictionrules for reps.
  • Predictable types include Lookup (up to 50 options per lookup), Boolean, Integer, Choice, Option Set, Currency and text. Add descriptions to improve predictions. Hierarchical lookups (for example Product family to Product) work only when the parent lookup column is in the child table's Quick Find Active view; main, system and custom views are not used.
  • Updates: Case creation and update > Case update by AI agent (any channel) > Create: rule name, conditions, Fields for AI prediction > Save > order rules (they run in listed order) > Activate. With no rule, no fields are updated autonomously. Allow AI agent to override human edits during autonomous updates controls overwriting.
  • Creation: Case creation by AI agent (from chats and voice) > make the agent available (the label still says Case Processing Agent) and pick fields; it fires when a rep accepts or ends a conversation and only if there is enough context.
  • Experience profile: Copilot AI features > From conversations (default profiles already allow it).
  • Test before go-live: Go to simulation (up to 100 case records, or an Excel file up to 1 MB and 100 records) and shadow mode; both use Copilot credits.

Case resolution

  • Configure Customer Intent Agent first; its lines of business appear under Level of automation per line of business (Case settings > Manage CMA > Case resolution > Edit).
  • Full: the agent emails the customer and resolves the case; Require agent confirmation: it drafts and a rep reviews and sends; Shadow mode: predicted actions are evaluated on live cases without sending emails or updating records; Disabled: no drafts. Simulation runs only for a Disabled line of business.
  • Full autonomy: in the Power Platform admin center create an application user with the Customer Service Representative role, create a shared mailbox in the Microsoft 365 admin center and set its address on the application user, then set Application user in the Case resolution settings.
  • Language settings: Use case record (a locale field such as en-US) or A single language; if no language is found, the agent hands off to a rep.
  • Triggers: an inbound email whose Regarding is a case, a closed conversation transcript regarding a case, or the business event msdyn_invokeCaseProcessingAgent called by plug-ins, flows or external systems.

Case follow-up and closure

  1. Optional: Email template groups.
  2. Case settings > Manage CMA > Case follow-up and closure > Turn on the case follow-up and closure automation > Add a rule.
  3. Set rule name, conditions, level of automation, at least one Follow-up trigger (based on context, or on status reason), Number of follow-ups (a rep's unanswered email counts as the first), Follow-up wait times and templates; Save.
  4. Select the rule and Activate. Optionally tick Let Copilot fill out resolution details (with Manage data sources).

The rollout manager (Agent hub > Create a rollout plan) phases in autonomous agents; for CMA only, deactivating or deleting a plan also deactivates or deletes its rules.

Exam traps
  • Mode names differ by page: Semi-autonomous and Fully autonomous (overview), Full / Require agent confirmation / Shadow mode / Disabled (resolution), Require human confirmation / Full automation (closure).
  • CMA creates and updates cases from authenticated chats only; unauthenticated chat does not qualify.
  • Require agent confirmation and shadow mode never send emails by themselves; only Full does, and only with an application user plus shared mailbox.
  • Hierarchical lookup depends on the Quick Find Active view of the child table.
  • Resolution needs Customer Intent Agent; Enable AI agents lives in the Power Platform admin center, not in Copilot Service admin center.

Integrate agents with Customer Service, including plug-ins and knowledge sources

GoalIntegration path
Add tools, knowledge or agents to Ask a questionExtend Copilot with Copilot Studio (Customer Support agent > Extend agent tab)
Self-service Copilot agent on chat, voice or digital channelsAdd a Copilot Studio agent to a push-based workstream in Copilot Service admin center (§2.1)
Give the Case Management Agent your own logicCustom Copilot Studio agent linked to an intent
Extend Service Agent in Microsoft 365 CopilotMaker mode: Copilot Studio agent or non-Microsoft MCP server

Extend Copilot with Copilot Studio Preview

  • A production-ready preview; since April 2026 extensibility is configured mainly in Copilot Studio. Needs System Administrator or Customer Service administrator, Copilot credits and Copilot enabled. Not in GCC-M or GCC-H.
  • Enable: Copilot Service admin center > Productivity > Copilot settings > Manage > Customer Support > Settings > Extend agent tab > Extend agent with Copilot Studio > Save. The tab also holds custom context (entity, data field, description) on top of the default context (current record, user role, session metadata) and the link to the managed agent Customer Service Copilot Bot.
  • Evaluation order: Copilot checks whether extensibility is on, sends the request and context to the Copilot Studio agent, shows its answer if confident, otherwise falls back to its configured knowledge sources. Rephrasing, summarization and translation take priority.
  • Types: Knowledge (SharePoint, public sites), Tools (for example an MCP server or custom connector), Agents and Topics. You can't change the agent model, its Instructions, managed msdyn_ topics, or custom connectors that use OAuth.
  • Plug-ins: existing plugins keep working and are managed as tools. To update one, find its tool in Customer Service Copilot Bot and edit it; for changes beyond the connection or tool description, create a new tool and remove the old one. Dynamics context for a tool is added as custom context in Copilot Service admin center. Targeted phrases that call plugins from Ask a question are labelled preview.
  • Copilot Studio knowledge sources: public website, documents, SharePoint, Dataverse and connectors (the last three use the signed-in user's Microsoft Entra identity).

Copilot Studio agent on a channel

  • Create the agent in Copilot Service admin center or Copilot Studio, connect it to omnichannel, select it in the workstream, add it to a queue and configure context variables. One agent per workstream, and agents receive conversations only in push-based workstreams. Include an escalation topic and an end-of-conversation topic; a conversation also closes after 30 minutes of inactivity.
  • Roles: CCI Admin (to open the agent in Copilot Studio) and Omnichannel administrator.
  • Knowledge management for agents (§1.2): enable Dataverse search (System Administrator), set the Microsoft Dataverse and Content Conversion connection references, turn on the Search Dynamics 365 knowledge article flow, then use the Search Dynamics 365 knowledge articles action; the default search covers published external articles (statecode eq 3 and isinternal eq false).

Case Management Agent and Service Agent

  • CMA calls a custom Copilot Studio agent linked to an intent when autonomous resolution and intent are enabled. It sends {"caseId":"<id>"}; the agent replies with responseType of Question, Resolved, UnableToResolve, NoAction or ResolveCase, plus an optional message.
  • Service Agent (GA as a Microsoft 365 Copilot agent): a Microsoft 365 admin manages the Service app, which installs automatically with a Customer Service license; a Dynamics admin adds Microsoft Copilot to the environment. In maker mode (scope Organization, Application profile or User) you add a published Copilot Studio agent (Agent ID and Environment ID, plus a clear description) or a non-Microsoft MCP server (Display name, Name, Endpoint URL, API scope, Tool prefix; the endpoint must support Microsoft Entra authentication). It needs the prvmsdyn_ServiceAgentMakerCustomize privilege on msdyn_agentmetadataoverride.
Exam traps
  • "Plugins" in Copilot are managed as Copilot Studio tools; they are not Dataverse C# plug-ins.
  • If Copilot Studio gives no confident answer, Copilot falls back to knowledge sources; it does not error out.
  • Service Agent maker mode and the Extend agent tab are different surfaces for different agents.
  • One agent per workstream, and only push-based workstreams deliver conversations to it.

Sources: Help pane · Copilot features · Use Copilot filters · Ask a question · Verbatim responses · Summaries · Case summary · Custom forms · Customize conversation summaries · Timeline control · Enable Copilot to draft emails · Draft emails with Copilot · Contact Center deprecations · CMA settings · Case creation and update · Case resolution · Follow-up and closure · Rollout plans · Extend Copilot · Integrate a Copilot agent · Agent knowledge · CMA custom agents · Service Agent: Copilot Studio agents · Service Agent: MCP servers · Copilot Studio knowledge sources

sections.title: 1.5 Create and manage SLAs for cases
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure SLA settings • Implement actions by using Power Automate • Apply SLAs • Create and manage SLA items, KPIs, warning and success actions and applicability • Configure a timer control on a form • Create SLA KPIs. Practise by building one SLA end to end: a KPI, an SLA with an item, a warning and a failure action in Power Automate, set it as the default, and add the SLA Timer to the case form.

Configure SLA settings

Service level agreements (SLAs) track whether work such as a first response or a resolution happens on time. Everything lives under Copilot Service admin center > Operations > Service terms, which has the sections Entitlements, Service-level agreements, SLA KPIs and Other SLA Settings (Manage opens Service Configuration Settings).

CapabilityWeb-client SLAs (standard or enhanced)Unified Interface SLAs
TablesStandard: Case only. Enhanced: any SLA-enabled table.Any SLA-enabled table.
ActionsWorkflows: Send Email, Create Record, Update Record, Assign Record, Change StatusWorkflows and Power Automate flows
Pause and resumeStandard SLAs can't pause. Enhanced: table-level pause only.Table, KPI and SLA item levels
Business hours (calendar)On the SLAOn the SLA item
KPIsNo parallel KPIs; one Applicable From for the SLAParallel KPIs; Applicable From per KPI
Custom time calculation, forced recalculationNot supportedSupported

Web-client SLAs were deprecated on October 1, 2020; migrate them to Unified Interface SLAs. Both kinds appear in the list but can be edited only where they were created.

Enable a table for SLAs

  1. Power Apps > Solutions > Default Solution > Tables > the table > Properties > Advanced options > select Setting up service level agreements > Save.
  2. Advanced > Publish table, then Publish all customizations.
  3. For a custom table or activity, also add a lookup column to SLA KPI Instance so each KPI instance can be stored on the record.

Supported tables include Account, Contact, Order, Invoice, Quote, Opportunity, Lead, activity tables (Email, Phone Call, Appointment; not Recurring Appointment) and custom tables.

LimitValue
Tables with active SLAs7
SLA KPIs per table5 recommended
SLA items per SLA tableMaximum 100; fewer than 15 recommended
RegionSLAs are not supported in Singapore

Service Configuration Settings

SettingEffect
Disable SLAsEnabled by default. Yes: SLAs can still be created or edited but are not applied (use for maintenance or data imports).
Recalculate SLA on terminal statusRe-evaluates Applicable When and Success for instances that are already Succeeded or Noncompliant (the two states Microsoft's recalculation steps describe).
Apply SLA after manual overrideNo: after an SLA was applied manually, an entitlement or default SLA is not applied automatically on update.
Select SLA Pause StatusPer SLA-enabled table, the statuses that pause SLA calculation (the table-level pause).
Automatically apply entitlementApplies the customer's default entitlement when a case is created, and on update when the customer, contact or product changes.
Calendar Export and ImportExports or imports the holiday and customer service schedules with an SLA solution.

The same options appear on the legacy System Settings > Service tab, so page names vary.

Business hours, pause precedence and security

  • Business hours come from the customer service schedule: Operations > Calendar > Customer service calendar > Manage (work hours Are the same each day, Vary by day or 24 x 7; time zone; a Holiday Schedule that the customer service schedule observes). Associate the schedule with the SLA item (Business Hours). With no schedule, time counts all day, every day.
  • Pause conditions can be set at three levels, and the most specific one wins: SLA item (Override Criteria) > SLA KPI (Override Criteria) > table (Select SLA Pause Status). They are not combined. Override Criteria = Yes is needed, and Allow Pause and Resume must be enabled on the General tab. A KPI without pause conditions of its own keeps the table-level setting.
  • Security: admins need the CSR Manager role or equivalent permissions on SLA, SLA KPI, SLA KPI Instance, Connector and Process Stage Parameter; reps need the Customer Service Representative role plus read access to SLA, SLA KPI and SLA KPI instance. Whoever activates the SLA monitoring flow and SLA action flows needs the global prvReadSLAKPIInstance and prvWriteSLAKPIInstance privileges. Don't customize the SLA admin forms.
  • Advanced: call the custom action msdyn_ManageSLAInstances with Recalculate = 1 (default 0) from plug-in code to force recalculation of In Progress and Nearing noncompliance instances. Custom time calculation uses the template SLACustomTimeCalculationTemplate plus the SLA item toggle Allow Custom Time Calculation (plug-in only; inputs ApplicableFrom, CalendarId and Duration in minutes).
  • Limitations: Applicable When and Success conditions on related tables misbehave; avoid Modified On; no two items with the same Applicable When and KPI; SLA time can't be edited by hand; an SLA already assigned to a case can't be edited or removed.
Exam traps
  • Seven tables with active SLAs, five KPIs per table and 100 items (fewer than 15 advised) are three different numbers.
  • Standard SLAs are Case only and can't pause; anything for other tables or with pause and resume needs enhanced or Unified Interface SLAs.
  • Pause precedence is item, then KPI, then table. A pause status chosen at table level is overridden by a KPI or item.
  • Disable SLAs stops SLAs from being applied but does not delete or block editing them.
  • The settings page has several names: Other SLA Settings, Service Configuration Settings and the System Settings Service tab.

Implement actions by using Power Automate

Unified Interface SLAs use out-of-the-box actions in Power Automate. Each SLA item has a predefined cloud flow with a Switch control, and you add actions inside its branches.

BranchRuns whenTypical action
Is Nearing Non-Compliance (shown as [Do not delete or update] Is Nearing Non-Compliance)Warning time is reachedWarning email to the owner or a manager
Is SucceededThe success condition is metNotification or follow-up update
Is Non-compliantFailure time passesEscalate: update the record, assign, send an email
  1. Open the SLA > select the SLA item > Edit SLA Item > Actions > Configure Actions. Power Automate opens in a new tab.
  2. Accept the connection (or select the ellipsis and fix it) > Continue. The predefined flow opens; don't edit the flow itself.
  3. In the Switch control choose the branch, then Add an action.
  4. To send an email choose Perform an unbound action, set Action Name to msdyn_SendEmailFromTemplate and fill in From, To Item, Cc Item, Regarding and Template.
  5. Repeat for the other branches > Save and exit > Save & Close the SLA item > Activate the SLA.

The monitoring flow and platform limits

  • The SLA monitoring cloud flow must be on. If it is off, KPI instances never reach Nearing noncompliance or Noncompliant, and the timer shows a message that the SLA instances might be incorrect because the workflow is turned off. Activating a Unified Interface SLA turns it on when no SLA is active; otherwise turn it on in Power Automate > My flows > Cloud flows (global prvReadSLAKPIInstance and prvWriteSLAKPIInstance needed). Learn spells the flow name two ways (SLAInstanceMonitoringWarningAndExpiryFlow on the define-SLA and troubleshooting pages, SLAWarningAndExpiryMonitoringFlow on the timer page), so know the behaviour rather than the exact name.
  • SLAs are subject to Power Automate platform limits (action bursts).
Web-client (classic) itemUnified Interface item
Success Action, Failure Actions and Warning Actions built from workflow stepsThe three Power Automate branches
Steps limited to five types: Send Email, Create Record, Update Record, Assign Record, Change StatusAny action Power Automate offers
Failure and warning actions run asynchronously and may not fire exactly on time; under one hour can be delayed. Save the item before adding them.Time is tracked by the monitoring flow
Exam traps
  • Warning maps to Is Nearing Non-Compliance, success to Is Succeeded and failure to Is Non-compliant.
  • The email is an unbound action called msdyn_SendEmailFromTemplate; a bound action or the Send an email (V2) connector action is not the documented route.
  • Edit the branches only. Editing the predefined flow itself can stop SLAs from working.
  • With the monitoring flow off, warning and failure actions never run.

Apply SLAs

MethodHow it worksKey point
AutomaticA workflow, a Power Automate flow or a custom plug-in sets the SLA on the recordUse it for rules such as "SLA by customer country"; a pre-update plug-in sets incident["slaid"] to an EntityReference of the SLA
EntitlementThe case's entitlement has an SLA lookupCase only; the entitlement must be activated; the Automatically apply entitlement setting controls it
ManualA rep chooses the SLA in the SLA fieldThe SLA field is not on the form by default; an admin adds it
Default SLASet As Default on the SLA ribbonFor Case, applies to cases with no entitlement SLA; other tables get one default each
  • Set As Default: Service terms > SLAs > Manage > select the SLA > Set As Default. Reactivate a deactivated default SLA before you set it again.
  • Entitlements: Service terms > Entitlements > Manage > New (from a template or blank); the SLA field ties the SLA and its KPIs to the support terms; set a default entitlement with Set As Default.
  • Only one SLA applies to a record. Applying a different SLA cancels the earlier one.
  • The Apply SLAs page lists the lookup order as automatic, then entitlement, then default. The system setting Apply SLA after manual override separately states that a manual SLA takes precedence, so know both statements.
  • An SLA is re-applied when an updated field is part of Applicable When. Matching items are re-evaluated, and failure or warning actions fire if the time is already exceeded.
  • Terminal status (the recalculation page lists Succeeded, Canceled and Noncompliant, but its steps describe only Succeeded and Noncompliant instances): Applicable When and Success are not re-evaluated by default. Turn on Recalculate SLA on terminal status; re-evaluation creates a new SLA KPI instance and cancels the old one (not for legacy SLAs).
  • Recalculation rules: a Succeeded instance changes with success-condition edits only when recalculation is Yes; a Noncompliant instance stays Noncompliant even when it is Yes; an Applicable When change recalculates Succeeded and Noncompliant instances when it is Yes, and the instance is Canceled if Applicable When is no longer met; an SLA item change creates a new instance (Expired if the failure time has already passed).
  • On the case form: a standard SLA saves only the failure time (a timer is optional); an enhanced SLA creates KPI instances with a timer. Putting the case on hold sets the instance to Paused; on resume the failure, warning and total hold times are updated if the SLA wasn't violated.
RequirementUse
Different SLA per customer country, no rep action, no entitlementsAutomatic: Power Automate flow, workflow or plug-in
SLA tied to a customer's contractEntitlement (Case only)
Fallback when no entitlement existsDefault SLA
Rep picks an SLA ad hocManual (add the SLA field to the form)
Exam traps
  • Entitlements apply to cases only; for other tables use automatic or default.
  • A record holds one SLA at a time; the default SLA is only a fallback.
  • Rep-selected SLAs need the SLA field added to the form first.
  • Closed (terminal) instances are not re-evaluated unless Recalculate SLA on terminal status is on, and a Noncompliant instance stays Noncompliant when the success condition changes.

Create and manage SLA items including key performance indicators (KPIs), warning actions, success actions, and applicability

ObjectRole
SLA KPIThe metric (for example First Response By) and the lookup field that stores it; holds Applicable From
SLAThe container for one primary table; holds the items
SLA itemOne rule: KPI, Applicable When, Success Conditions, durations, pause and actions
SLA KPI instanceThe runtime record created when an item applies to a record

Build order

  1. Create the SLA KPI.
  2. Service terms > SLAs > Manage > New: Name, Primary Entity, Description > Save. The SLA Items section now appears.
  3. New SLA Item, General tab: Name, KPI, Allow Pause and Resume (optional, and can't be toggled after the first save) and Business Hours (optional).
  4. Complete Applicable When, Success Conditions, Pause Configurations (only when pause is enabled: Override Criteria > Add), Warn and Fail Duration and Actions. Save.
  5. Edit the item > Configure Actions in Power Automate > Save & Close.
  6. Activate the SLA, then apply it (for example Set As Default).

Applicability, success and timing

  • Applicable When: the item runs when its condition is met; if it is no longer met, the KPI instance is canceled. Avoid frequently updated fields. Don't use the same attribute in Applicable When and in Success Conditions (a warning appears and the instance ends up Canceled).
  • Success Conditions: when met, the instance becomes Succeeded and the success branch runs.
  • Different targets for one KPI need separate items with different Applicable When conditions, for example High priority 2 hours and standard 8 hours. Identical Applicable When plus KPI isn't allowed.
  • A null warning duration skips Nearing noncompliance. Durations count business hours; a "1 day" duration means 24 hours consumed only inside working hours.
  • Classic items use Related Case Field (standard) or SLA KPI (enhanced), Success Criteria, Success Action, Failure After with Failure Actions and Warn After with Warning Actions. Standard SLAs apply only the first matching item per KPI. Classic SLAs of either type should have no more than 15 items per SLA (a performance recommendation, not a limit), and enhanced SLAs shouldn't have their SLA KPI Instance values updated directly by plug-ins or processes.
Instance stateWhen
In progressApplied and the timer is running
Nearing noncomplianceWarning time reached (yellow)
NoncompliantFailure time passed (red; negative countdown)
SucceededSuccess condition met
PausedA pause condition is true
CanceledApplicable When is no longer met; the SLA was reapplied or recalculated; or a pause then resume (the old instance is canceled and a new one created)

The terminal states are Succeeded, Canceled and Noncompliant. Manage SLAs by activating them after the items are saved; an SLA already assigned to a case can't be edited or removed.

Exam traps
  • Applicable From belongs to the KPI; Applicable When belongs to the item. Success Conditions decide the Succeeded state; success actions are the flow branch.
  • If a KPI instance becomes Canceled when a case is resolved, check for the same attribute (for example status) in Applicable When and Success.
  • Allow Pause and Resume cannot be changed once the item is saved.
  • Leave the warning duration empty (null) when you don't want a warning stage.

Configure a timer control on a form

ApproachUsed forKey settings
SLA Timer subgrid on the Case formCase with Unified Interface SLAsTable SLA KPI Instances (Regarding); default view All SLA KPI Instances; component SLA Timer; update frequency (default 30 minutes); Turn on negative countdown; Customized Labels
Quick view form with a TimerOther tables with enhanced SLAsLookup to SLA KPI Instance; a quick view per KPI instance field with a Timer; add the quick view control to the Main form
Legacy Timer controlClassic form designerSwitch to classic > Insert > Timer; required Name, Label, Failure Time Field and Success Condition; optional Warning Condition and Cancel Condition; form body only, not the header

Add the SLA Timer to the case form

  1. Configure the KPIs, SLAs and items first.
  2. Power Apps > the Case table > the Case for interactive experience form > add a subgrid component.
  3. Set Table to SLA KPI Instances (Regarding) and the default view to All SLA KPI Instances.
  4. Components > add component > SLA Timer.
  5. Set the update frequency (30 minutes by default; avoid very short values), Turn on negative countdown = Yes to show overdue time, and Customized Labels > bind to a table column (for example Resolution) > Done.
  6. Save and publish.

Runtime behaviour

  • The timer shows only KPIs created with Unified Interface SLAs, and No Applicable SLA when none applies.
  • Statuses: In progress, Noncompliant, Nearing noncompliance, Paused, Succeeded, Canceled. Pause and resume refresh automatically; other changes need Refresh. Overdue time counts up only when negative countdown is configured.
  • The quick view Timer shows Succeeded, Expired, Paused, Canceled or Not Set, turns yellow near noncompliance and red, counting up, after expiry.
  • The legacy Timer works independent of SLAs: it shows state or remaining and elapsed time against the Failure Time field and doesn't calculate pause time.
Exam traps
  • The SLA Timer subgrid and the legacy Timer control are different controls with different required settings.
  • Reps can't see overdue time until Turn on negative countdown is set to Yes.
  • The default update interval is 30 minutes, not real time.
  • No Applicable SLA can mean no matching SLA, or a web-client SLA that the timer doesn't show.

Create SLA KPIs

A KPI is the indicator an SLA measures, such as First Response or Resolve By. The KPI's KPI Field is a lookup column on the target table that points to SLA KPI Instance.

  1. For a custom indicator, first add a lookup column on the target table that targets SLA KPI Instance (for example EscalatedByKPI). The Case table already has KPI lookup fields such as FirstResponseByKPI; other tables need new lookups.
  2. Copilot Service admin center > Operations > Service terms > SLA KPIs > Manage > Active SLAKPIs > New.
  3. General tab: Name, Owner, Entity Name, KPI Field (the lookup) and Applicable From (for example Created On).
  4. Save.
  5. Optional: Pause Conditions (Override Criteria = Yes > Add).
  6. Activate.
  • Failure Time, Warning Time and Applicable From fields must be DateTime, not Date.
  • Pausing then resuming cancels the instance and creates a new one.
  • For tables other than Case the Regarding column on the KPI instance shows blank by design.
  • In Unified Interface SLAs Applicable From is set on the KPI; in classic SLAs it is set on the SLA, so KPIs can't differ. Different start moments need different KPIs.
  • KPI instance fields include name, status, regarding, failure time, warning time and succeeded on. Active Duration (min) shows only when Paused or terminal; Elapsed Time (min) only when In progress or terminal.
Exam traps
  • KPI, KPI instance and SLA item are different objects: the KPI defines the metric, the instance is the runtime record, the item carries the rules.
  • The KPI Field must be a lookup to SLA KPI Instance. A DateTime column is used for failure, warning and applicable-from times, not as the KPI Field.
  • A KPI-level pause is configured through Override Criteria, not by editing the item.
