sections.title: 2.1 Configure routing
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure workstreams • configure user settings • manage capacity profiles • configure work classification and assignments, including rules • configure basic routing rulesets • configure skills-based routing and skill finder models • configure queues • configure routing for records. Practise by building one unified routing path end to end: reps as bookable resources, a chat or record workstream, a queue, a classification rule, a route-to-queue rule, a capacity profile and a skill, then send a test item through it.

Configure workstreams

Unified routing is configured in the Copilot Service admin center (formerly Customer Service admin center) and delivers work to the Copilot Service workspace; older pages still say "human agent" for the representative. A workstream is the container that enriches, routes and assigns work items. One workstream can serve several channels of the same type, and every conversation from them inherits its routing and assignment settings. You need the System Administrator role or permission to access and modify secure columns.

Workstream typeRoutes
MessagingLive chat, SMS, social and Microsoft Teams conversations (pick the channel; for Chat the Make chats persistent check box appears)
RecordRecords such as case, email and activity (pick the record type; unified routing must be turned on first)
VoiceCalls to the support phone numbers (Push is the only work distribution mode)
  1. Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > Workstreams > New workstream; enter the Name, Type and the Channel (Messaging) or Record type.
  2. Choose the Work distribution mode, Push or Pick. You can't edit it later; create a new workstream to change it.
  3. Set the Fallback queue: Create new (add its users after the workstream exists) or Choose existing (the default is the out-of-the-box queue for the channel type).
  4. Select Create, then configure the channel instance (chat widget, voice, WhatsApp, SMS, record routing and so on).
ModeWhat it means
PushThe system routes the item to a rep automatically with a message alert (it can be configured so the rep must explicitly pick it up). Voice, AI agents, representative affinity and preferred representative routing all need push workstreams.
PickThe rep explicitly picks the item from Open work items.

Work distribution and advanced settings

  • Capacity: Unit based or Profile based. Allowed presences: the base statuses in which a rep can be assigned work; leave out Inactive and Do not disturb if reps who miss or reject a notification should not get new items.
  • Block capacity for wrap up: Always block (the default; capacity stays consumed until the conversation is closed), Don't block (released as soon as the conversation moves to Wrap-up) or Custom time (30 seconds to 60 minutes). With an End of day capacity profile the wrap-up duration does not reset the capacity.
  • Default skill matching algorithm: Exact Match, Closest Match or None (behaviour is covered under skills-based routing).
  • Keep same representative for entire conversation (representative affinity): a resumed conversation returns to the rep who handled it; push workstreams only. For persistent chat also tick Make chats persistent when you create the workstream.
  • Advanced settings: Sessions, Representative notifications (a template per notification type), Context variables, Smart assist agents (case and knowledge suggestions via smart assist are deprecated), Quick replies and the live conversation counter. Session templates are covered in §2.3.
  • AI agent: in the Bot area select Add bot; the item goes to the agent first. Push workstreams only, and the docs advise against adding agents to record-routing workstreams.
  • Fallback queue: the per-workstream safety net that receives an item when classification fails, a route-to-queue rule errors, or no route-to-queue rule matches. It overrules any overflow settings. Any queue, even a default queue, can be the fallback; a new one uses the Highest capacity method and needs users. Before you delete a workstream, remove its intake rules and close its queue items and live work items.
Exam traps
  • Push or Pick can't be changed after creation, and voice supports Push only.
  • Fallback queue (per workstream; errors and no match; ignores overflow), default queues (system-defined; only the assignment method is editable) and overflow (hours, work item limit, wait time) are three separate things.
  • The Pick mode is not the queue assignment method No auto assignment.
  • Allowed presences lists base statuses only; a custom presence maps to one of them.

Configure user settings

Reps and supervisors are created and licensed in the Microsoft 365 admin center and must be configured as bookable resources before unified routing can assign work to them. Microsoft documents the per-user settings under Manage users, in two places:

Enhanced user management (bulk)Classic user page (one user)
WhereCustomer support > User management > Manage for Enhanced user managementUser management > Users > open the user > Omnichannel tab
What you setUpdate user attributes: Update skills, Update queues, Update capacity profiles, Update conversation limit (1–100)Capacity (units), Default Presence, New Bookable Resource, New Bookable Resource Characteristic (skill plus rating), queue membership
LimitsUp to 200 users and five attributes per step (save, then update the next set); the service-quotas page recommends 25 users per bulk updateOne user at a time
  • Capacity units: a rep's capacity must be a multiple of the workstream's capacity unit. Unit 1 and three simultaneous chats means 3; unit 5 and three chats means 15. Use capacity profiles or units in an organization, not both.
  • Timing: changes to skills, capacity profiles, calendars and routing settings can take up to 15 minutes to show in the user experience.
  • Bulk setup with Dataverse API calls, in this order: users → queues → bookable resources → skills → capacity profiles → roles. Submit about 500 change requests per 15 minutes; out-of-order or faster loads can leave user data inconsistent.

Presence

  • Base statuses (selectable in Allowed presences): Available, Busy, Busy-DND, Away, Offline. The out-of-the-box list adds Inactive, set by the system when a rep misses notifications; reps can't pick it. Out-of-the-box statuses can't be edited or deleted.
  • Default presence is the status a rep signs in with; if none is defined the application uses Available. Docs advise against reps and supervisors changing presence manually.
  • Custom presence: Support experience (older pages say Agent experience) > Productivity > Custom Presence > Manage > New: Name, Presence Text (shown to reps), Base Status and Description. Example: Away – In Training mapped to the Away base status.

Roles and personas

PersonaDefault role in Customer ServiceDefault role in Contact Center
AdminCSR ManagerOmnichannel Administrator
SupervisorCSR ManagerOmnichannel supervisor
Agent (representative)Customer Service RepresentativeOmnichannel agent
  • Persona mapping (User management > Manage for Role persona mapping) lets you add custom security roles to a persona. It needs the System Administrator role, the custom role needs the prvAgent, prvSupervisor or prvAdmin privilege, and the roles must be assigned directly to users, not through team membership. Mapping a role does not give users access to the related apps, dashboards or forms; grant that separately. Security roles are covered in §1.1.
Exam traps
  • Capacity units must be a multiple of the workstream's unit; a rep with capacity 4 on a workstream with unit 3 is misconfigured.
  • Allowed presences accepts base statuses only. Inactive is system-set and not selectable by reps.
  • Persona mapping ignores roles that reach a user through a team.
  • Bulk updates in the admin center are limited per step (five attributes); more changes need several steps.

Manage capacity profiles

A capacity profile defines how much work a rep can take (concurrent or daily) and whether other channels are affected. Reps can have several profiles, supervisors can override capacity, and capacity can show a negative value after a manual pick. Capacity isn't consumed when a rep only monitors a conversation. Reps must be bookable resources, and the workstream's Capacity must be Profile based.

  1. Customer support > User management > Manage for Capacity profile > Create new.
  2. Details tab: Profile name, Work item limit, Reset frequency and Assignment blocking.
  3. Users tab > Add user > select the reps > Add user.
SettingBehaviour
Reset frequencyImmediate: capacity is reset immediately, for example when a work item closes. End of day: capacity is reset after the rep's shift ends even if conversations are still open; those items don't count toward the limit and the rep gets new work next shift. You can edit every setting except reset frequency; recreate the profile to change it.
Assignment blocking = YesWhen the limit is reached the rep gets nothing automatically, even unit-based work and even if other profiles or units still have room. Presence becomes Busy-DND. The docs' use case is keeping other work away from a rep who is on a phone call.
Custom limitA different limit for selected reps (experienced vs new). It applies to new assignments only; work already assigned isn't reassigned. Reps without one follow the profile default.

Set a custom limit in Enhanced user management (select the reps > Update user attributes > Update capacity profiles > pick the profile and enter the Custom limit > Add to all > Save); clear the value to reset it. By code, set msdyn_maxunits on msdyn_bookableresourcecapacityprofile (null resets it):

var data = { msdyn_maxunits: 5 }; // the custom limit
Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord("msdyn_bookableresourcecapacityprofile", "<Bookable Resource Capacity Profile ID>", data);

Using profiles at run time

  • Set the profile in the workstream's work distribution (applies to every routed item) and/or have a classification rule append a profile through its Capacity profile output. When an item carries several profiles, assignment looks for a rep with capacity in all of them, and capacity is consumed from each. Docs example: a Total profile (five cases a day) is the workstream default; classification adds High (two a day) or Normal (four a day). Reps need all three profiles, and all reset at end of day.
  • Release: a conversation frees capacity when the rep ends it and closes the session; a case when it is resolved, cancelled, or the rep clears Worked By on the queue item. For emails and other activities routed as records capacity is not released automatically: deactivate the queue item (the live work item closes), or clear Worked By to keep the record open.
  • The escalation profile is out of the box, can't be edited, and keeps a rep from new chats or calls while a chat escalated to voice or video is in progress.
Exam traps
  • Reset frequency is the one profile setting that can't be edited after creation.
  • Capacity for routed emails and other activities isn't released automatically; deactivate the queue item or clear Worked By.
  • A custom limit never reassigns work that is already assigned.
  • Assignment blocking sets presence to Busy-DND; it doesn't release capacity.

Configure work classification and assignments, including rules

Routing runs in two stages: classification (rules or machine learning) enriches the item, then assignment prioritises the queued items and matches reps on skills, presence and capacity. Know which rule family does which job:

Rule familyLives onJob
Intake ruleRecord routing / workstreamChooses the workstream (or active basic routing rule) for an incoming record
Work classification rulesetWorkstream > Routing rulesSets output attributes on the item, such as skills or a capacity profile
Route-to-queue rulesetWorkstream > Routing rulesChooses the queue
Prioritization rulesetQueue (custom assignment)Orders items inside one queue
Assignment rulesetQueue (custom assignment)Chooses and orders the reps
Queue priority numberQueueRanks queues against each other for reps who belong to several

Work classification rulesets

  • Workstream > Routing rules > Work classification (optional) > Create Ruleset > Create new; Rule type = Logical rules or Machine learning model; start from a Template ruleset (read-only in the workstream), Copy from template or New ruleset. Needs the CSR Manager or Omnichannel administrator role.
  • A rule reads “if the conditions match, set these outputs”: up to five output attributes per rule item, for example Skill or Capacity profile (a machine learning ruleset uses a published skill finder model). Limits: 10 rulesets per workstream, 100 rule items per ruleset.
  • Evaluation: classification rulesets run first, in list order, then the route-to-queue ruleset. Within a ruleset when one rule item matches, its output runs and control passes to the next ruleset, which can use the values set earlier.

Route-to-queue rulesets

  • A workstream has one route-to-queue ruleset (up to 200 rules). No rules or no match sends the item to the fallback queue.
  • Hit-all (the default policy) evaluates the rule conditions and the queues' overflow state: with several matches the first queue that isn't overflowing wins. Hit-first stops at the first match whatever the overflow state.
  • Percentage-based allocation splits work across up to five queues (the percentages sum to 100), for example between two vendors. Overflow is evaluated after the percentage picks a queue.

Assignment methods

Set on the queue (Advanced queues > the queue > Assignment method):

MethodHow it picks the repNotes
Highest capacityMatches skills, allowed presence and capacity; most available capacity firstHonors the workstream's Default skill matching algorithm
Advanced round robinOrder starts with when a rep joined the queue, then follows the last assignment; kept per queueSpreads work fairly
Least activeThe rep who has been least active (last capacity-release time)Voice and messaging queues only; the default for a new voice or messaging queue
No auto assignmentItems wait until a rep picks them from the Inbox or a supervisor assigns themNot the same as the Pick workstream mode
Create newYour own prioritization and assignment rulesetsYou write presence, capacity and skill rules yourself

Custom assignment (Create new)

  • Prioritization ruleset: ordered rules, each a priority bucket (conditions plus Order by); unmatched items fall into the last bucket, first in first out. One per queue; it runs every assignment cycle. Without one the queue is first in first out.
  • Assignment rulesets: ordered rules whose conditions select reps and whose Order by (Least active, Round robin, unit- or profile-based available capacity, Proficiency, Skill count) sorts them; if no rep matches, the next rule is tried. With several rulesets, define selection criteria (Execute ruleset); if none match, the default ruleset runs.
  • Cautions: the workstream's presence, capacity and skill-matching defaults are not used, so write those conditions yourself (for example Presence status equals Conversation.Workstream.Allowed Presences). The default methods ignore working hours; use the is_working operator. Don't use rollup or calculated columns.
  • Assignment cycle triggers: a new item, a presence change, a runtime capacity change (a manual edit doesn't trigger it), a rep added to a queue, and every five minutes for records.

Templates, preferred representatives and status

  • Template rulesets (Routing > Templates): pick the type (Assignment, Prioritization or Work Classification), build the rules, Publish, then Assign template to workstreams (classification) or queues (assignment, prioritization), up to 10 at a time (five with context variables). Downstream copies are read-only; edit the template and republish.
  • Preferred representative routing: up to three reps per contact, tried in order; only presence is checked (capacity, skills and assignment rules are skipped); push workstreams only.
  • Status: sentiment prediction-based classification (the Sentiment prediction rule type) Preview, dynamic prioritization Preview and intent-driven routing (a production-ready preview) are preview features. The effort estimation model was deprecated and removed, and routing diagnostics is deprecated in favour of conversation diagnostics in Azure Application Insights.
Exam traps
  • In classification the first matching rule item per ruleset runs and then the next ruleset starts; route-to-queue is a single ruleset with Hit-all by default.
  • A smaller queue priority number wins. A prioritization ruleset orders items inside one queue; it does not rank queues.
  • Custom assignment does not inherit workstream defaults, so skill, presence and capacity checks must be written as conditions.
  • Least active is only for voice and messaging queues. Reps pick from the Inbox under No auto assignment.

Configure basic routing rulesets

Basic routing (the classic routing rule sets) routes cases only, to a queue, user or team. Microsoft recommends unified routing for automatic routing of records; basic routing suits simple case routing without skills or capacity. Roles: Customer Service Manager, System Administrator or System Customizer (or equivalent).

  1. Copilot Service admin center > Routing > Manage for Basic routing rule sets > New; enter a Name and Description and Save.
  2. In Rule Items select New Rule Item: Name and Description, then Rule Criteria (Add Row, Add Group, Add related entity).
  3. Action > Route to: choose a queue or a user/team, then Save & Close.
  4. Arrange the rule items in the order you want, then select Activate on the rule set record.
  • Rule items are evaluated top to bottom; the first one that is true routes the case and further evaluation stops.
  • When unified routing is not enabled, only one routing rule set can be active; activating another deactivates the current one. Deactivate a rule set before editing it.
  • Criteria limits (Unified Interface): one related-entity level, no one-to-many or many-to-many related entities, no Multi Select Option Set columns, no time value on Date and Time, and lookups allow only equal, not equal, null and not null.
  • Triggering: Save & Route on the case form, or select cases in a list and choose Apply Routing Rule. Whether a new case is routed automatically depends on its Route Case value (see the trigger table under routing for records).
  • Solutions: rule sets are solution-aware but their queue, user or team targets are not, so re-map the rule items after import (deactivate the rule set first).
  • After unified routing is turned on, the active basic routing rule no longer routes records until you create an intake rule and map it to a workstream or to that active basic routing rule.
Exam traps
  • Basic routing handles only cases; emails, activities and custom records, skills and capacity need unified routing.
  • First true rule item wins; a later, more specific rule item never runs.
  • Without unified routing one rule set is active at a time, and a case created in the UI is not routed until you use Save & Route or Apply Routing Rule.
  • Enabling unified routing silently stops the active basic rule until an intake rule exists.

Configure skills-based routing and skill finder models

Skills, rating models and rating values are shared with other model-driven apps in the environment, such as Field Service and Project Service Automation. Skills can also be associated with an AI agent.

Setup order

  1. Create a rating model (Operations > Insights > Skill-based routing > Manage > Rating Model > New Rating Model: name, minimum and maximum, then a New Rating Value for each score; 1–10 is recommended).
  2. Create skill types and skills. The live setup page creates skill types in the classic Bookable Resource Characteristic Type option set (Advanced Settings > Customizations > Customize the system > Option Sets). Its Skills hub steps (User management > Manage Skills hub) cover creating skills and proficiency scales; the hub also holds skill finder models.
  3. Assign reps to skills with a proficiency value.
  4. Set the workstream's Default skill matching algorithm (Exact Match or Closest Match).
  5. Attach skills to items with logical classification rules, or with an intelligent skill finder (ISF) model plus machine learning classification rules.
  6. Choose an out-of-the-box or custom assignment method on the queue.
  7. Enable skill control so reps can update skills.
Exact matchClosest match
RuleReps whose rating is greater than or equal to the required value on the skills; then ordered by the assignment methodAll reps ranked by closeness: exact-skill, over-qualified, then under-qualified
No qualified repThe item stays unassigned in the queueThe item might go to a rep with none of the required skills
Custom assignmentRule: User skills > Exact match > All skills (or a skill type)Order by Proficiency (Nearest Proficient) or Skill count; no filter rule needed

The workstream's algorithm applies only to out-of-the-box assignment; with custom assignment you write the conditions. Either way you must configure skill attachment rules so items carry skills. Use one rating model across skills; different models are normalised.

Model a table as skills

If the attribute already lives in a table (for example a product), add a Lookup column to the Characteristic table and to the Skill Main Form, create a skill of Type = Skill with the lookup value, assign it to reps, and use it in a custom assignment rule; no classification rule per skill is needed. Out-of-the-box assignment doesn't support modelled skills, and order by proficiency isn't supported.

Intelligent skill finder model

ISF trains a custom AI Builder category classification model on your history to predict skills for new items. AI Builder must be available in the region and AI Builder preview models must be enabled. A model trained in a test environment works only in another test environment, not production.

  1. Operations > Insights > Intelligent skill finder > Manage > New; enter a name.
  2. Data criteria: Attributes (required), optional Filters and a Date range; Save, then Load training data.
  3. Review the records, select Input data and Approve: at least 50 records are required.
  4. Train model; when training is completed, select the rows and Publish model.
  • No history? Use Import from Excel on the Training data tab: msdyn_ocsitrainingdata.csv first, then msdyn_ocsitdskill.csv, one at a time; input text up to 5,000 characters.
  • Attach the model with a classification ruleset whose Rule type is Machine learning model. Reps can correct skills at run time (User management > Manage Skill-based routing > Enable update skill control = Yes; on for messaging channels by default, records need a form customization); the corrections feed retraining.
Exam traps
  • Exact match means rating greater than or equal to the requirement on every skill, and no match means the item waits; closest match can assign to a rep without the skills.
  • The workstream's Default skill matching algorithm is silently ignored under custom assignment.
  • ISF needs AI Builder in the region with preview models enabled, and training needs at least 50 approved records.
  • Modelled-table skills need a Lookup column on Characteristic and a custom assignment rule.

Configure queues

Queues collect work and distribute it to member reps through an assignment method. Advanced queue types: Messaging (live chat, SMS, social), Records (cases and emails; the dialog label may read Record) and Voice. Pickers show only queues of the workstream's channel type, so a chat can be transferred only to a messaging queue and a case only to a record queue.

  1. Customer support > Queues > Manage for Advanced queues > New: Name, Type, Queue priority > Create.
  2. Add users (bookable resources), then choose the Assignment method (Highest capacity, Advanced round robin, Least active, No auto assignment or Create new).
  3. Configure Overflow handling and Operation hours (an existing operating hour record; with none the queue is available around the clock).
  4. Optional: Metrics Threshold > Add Threshold: Service Level Threshold and Short Abandoned Threshold, in seconds.
  • Queue priority: a smaller number is a higher priority; it ranks queues when reps belong to several.
  • Default queues are system-defined (Default entity, Default messaging, Default voice); every rep with the Omnichannel agent role is a member and only the assignment method is editable. Microsoft recommends creating advanced queues instead.
Basic queueAdvanced queue
CreatedQueues > Manage Basic queues; Automatic work distribution = No (default); public or privateAutomatic work distribution = Yes on a basic queue, or Manage Advanced queues > New
MailboxYes, a mailbox record is createdNo mailbox; use basic queues for queue mailboxes
RevertingCan be changed to advancedCan't be reverted; create a new basic queue instead

Overflow handling

Overflow actions run before an item is queued or after it has waited. The before-queue check happens once per item, after the route-to-queue rules and before the item enters a queue (with an AI agent on the workstream, only after the agent escalates). Without overflow settings the item simply joins the queue.

WhenConditionChannels and range
Before queueingOut of operating hoursAll channels; added automatically (action Assign to queue anyway) when you set operation hours. You can't edit the condition, only its action.
Before queueingWork item limit exceedsVoice and messaging; 1–100
Before queueingAverage wait timeVoice only; 30 seconds to 60 minutes
After queueingWaiting time in queue exceedsVoice 1–60 minutes; messaging 1 minute–2 days; records 3 minutes–2 days
  • Actions: Assign to queue anyway; Transfer to a different queue; End conversation (messaging); End call, Direct callback, Voicemail, Transfer to an external number (voice only). Record queues support only Assign to queue anyway and Transfer to a different queue.
  • The workstream's channel operating hours do not drive overflow; the queue's own operation hours do.
  • Rule-specific overflow: on a route-to-queue rule, queue > More commands > Handle rule-specific overflows, for example so a priority customer's call isn't ended or left waiting.
  • A conversation sent to a queue with no reps is closed; records stay in the queue unassigned.
Exam traps
  • Automatic work distribution = Yes is one-way; an advanced queue can't have a mailbox.
  • A queue without operation hours is open around the clock; removing hours doesn't close it.
  • Average wait time is voice only; voicemail, callback, end call and external number are voice only.
  • Default queues (system-defined, only the assignment method is editable) are not the same as the workstream's fallback queue, which skips overflow.

Configure routing for records

Unified routing for records sends cases, emails and other activities through a record workstream. It needs unified routing enabled, the table enabled for queues, the System Administrator role, and reps configured as bookable resources.

  1. Enable unified routing: Routing > Manage for Manage unified routing > Unified routing = Yes > Save. It is off by default when only Customer Service is installed, and needs the Administrator role, CSR or CSR Manager, System Administrator on the root business unit and Read-Write CAL access. It imports a solution, so test outside production.
  2. Enable the table for queues: Power Apps > Tables > the table > Properties > Advanced options > Can be added to a queue; it can't be disabled afterwards. If When the rows are created or assigned, move them to the owner's default queue is on, records are not distributed; clear it.
  3. Create the reps' bookable resources and a Record queue.
  4. Routing > Manage for Record routing > Add > pick the record type; create the record workstream (Type = Record, Push or Pick) with its work distribution settings.
  5. Create an intake rule (workstream > Intake rules > Create rule): conditions on up to two levels of related records, mapped to a workstream or an active basic routing rule; reorder them in the decision list (maximum 100).
  6. Add classification and route-to-queue rules and a queue assignment method, then trigger routing.
TriggerHow
ManualSave & Route on the record form, or Apply Routing Rule on a list (not shown for Activities)
Cases, automaticCases created programmatically default to RouteCase = Yes and route on create; cases created in the user interface default to Route Case = No. A Route Case = No column suppresses routing on import.
Other records, automaticPower Automate flow: Dataverse trigger When a row is added, modified or deleted (docs example: table Email Messages, Scope Organization), then Perform an unbound action with Action Name msdyn_ApplyRoutingRuleEntityRecord and Target emails(<email id>) (entity collection name, from LogicalCollectionName)
  • Email as a case: set up rules to create or update records automatically, then save and route the case. Email as a record: a dedicated mailbox with server-side synchronization (creates the email record and its queue item), a routing flow, a record workstream with classification and route-to-queue rules, an intake rule and queues with assignment methods.
  • Objects: routing creates a live work item (msdyn_ocliveworkitem) holding allowed presence, matched skills and available capacity and, once queued, a queueitem. Updates synchronise from the queue item to the live work item, not the reverse; update one queue item field at a time.
  • Queue changes: advanced to advanced unassigns the rep and re-routes; advanced to basic closes the live work item; basic to advanced needs Save & Route. Deactivating the queue item closes the live work item; to reopen the record use Save & Route, never reactivate the queue item.
  • A rep without permission to a routed record can pick or be assigned its work item but can't view the record, and the conversation is closed. The case-form Assign option is Preview and off by default.
Exam traps
  • Can be added to a queue can't be switched off, and the owner-default-queue option blocks distribution.
  • Intake rules choose the workstream; classification enriches; route-to-queue chooses the queue.
  • The routing flow uses an unbound action, msdyn_ApplyRoutingRuleEntityRecord, with the collection name (emails), not the logical name, in Target.
  • A reopened record needs Save & Route, not queue item reactivation.

sections.title: 2.2 Configure productivity tools
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure scripts, including slugs • create macros. Practise by building a chat script with a text step, a macro step and a script step, adding it to a session template (§2.3) with a default-script expression, and running it as a rep.

Configure scripts, including slugs

A script is an ordered list of steps that guides reps with approved wording for fewer errors, process adherence and lower handling time. It applies to Customer Service and Contact Center (standalone). Build it with the Productivity tools administrator role; reps and supervisors who run it need Productivity tools user.

  1. Copilot Service admin center > Support experience > Productivity > Scripts > Manage > New: Name, Unique Name, Language, Description; Save.
  2. In Script steps select New Script step: Name (shown to the rep; slugs allowed), Unique Name, Order (position of the step), Action Type; Save and Close, then Save.
  3. Support experience > Workspaces > Session templates > the template > Scripts tab > Add Existing script > Add > Save. A script loads only for session types whose template lists it.
  4. Check that Agent scripts is on in the Productivity pane of the reps' experience profile.

Unique Name (scripts, steps, session templates): <prefix>_<name>, prefix alphanumeric only, 3 to 8 characters, underscore required, for example Contoso_script.

Action TypeExtra fieldRep seesUse when
Text instructionText instruction (slugs, OData)Mark as doneThe rep must say or check something (greeting, identity check)
MacroTarget macroRunOne click should act (open a pre-filled form, draft an email)
ScriptTarget scriptViewBranch to another script, which replaces the current one in the script menu

A green tick or red cross shows each step's last run.

Default script

To pick the starting script by context: session template > Scripts tab > Enable build expression = Yes > Build Expression. In the expression builder add a Condition; under If true select Add an action > Customer Service tab > Set default script and choose the script; repeat for If false; Save and close. Reps can still switch scripts manually.

Slugs, OData and static values

The automation dictionary holds the session's context data. A slug is a replacement parameter filled at run time from the channel provider, user actions, Dataverse or (macros only) earlier macro actions. Formats: slugs, OData queries, static (hard-coded) values.

WhereFormatExamples
Macros, scripts, default-script condition${slug}${customerName}, ${caseId}, ${queueId}
Record in the anchor tab${anchor.<attribute>}${anchor.ticketnumber} (case number), ${anchor.incidentid} (GUID)
Session or Omnichannel connector context${$session.<slug>}, ${$oc.<slug>}${$session.customerName}
Templates (session title, notification, application tab){slug}{customerName}, {anchor.<attribute>}
Value from Dataverse{$odata.<entityName>.<entityAttributeName>.<?options>}{$odata.incident.title.?$filter=incidentid eq '{caseId}'&$select=title}
Static valueHard-coded textNotification title New chat request
  • ${caseId} and ${caseTitle} resolve only when a case is linked to the conversation; ${customerEntityName} and ${customerRecordId} only for an authenticated contact or account.
  • Session.CurrentTab, Session.AnchorTab (EntityName, EntityId) and earlier macro action output work in macros only, never in templates.
  • The dictionary page adds that only ${anchor.<attribute_name>} is supported in macros and scripts for Copilot Service workspace, although it lists conversation slugs.
Exam traps: scripts
  • A finished script does nothing until a session template's Scripts tab lists it; Order only sequences steps and never picks the default script.
  • The App Profile Manager Administrator role is for experience profiles, not for building scripts.
  • Dictionary rule: ${...} in macros and scripts, {...} in templates. Some Learn examples, such as the script step name Hi {customer}, drop the dollar sign; follow the dictionary rule.
  • ${anchor.ticketnumber} is the case number; ${anchor.incidentid} is the record GUID.
  • A Script-type step loads another script only when the rep selects View; it never sets the default script.

Create macros

A macro is a set of sequential actions that runs on demand and is reusable because its values come from the session context. Designing needs Productivity tools administrator or System Administrator; reps and supervisors who run macros need Productivity tools user or Customer Service representative.

  1. Support experience > Productivity > Macros > Manage > New; enter a name and description.
  2. Always begin with the Start macro execution step.
  3. Add actions from the connectors below and fill attribute names and values with slugs or OData.
  4. Reps run the macro from the Productivity pane, usually through a script step of type Macro, or an API call (runMacro).
ConnectorActions to know
Productivity automationOpen a new form to create a record; Open an existing record; Autofill form fields; Update an existing record; Save the record; Resolve a case; Execute JavaScript; Open an email form with predefined template; knowledge search and Open knowledge base article; Open a record grid; Clone current record; set focus to a script
SessionGet the current tab; Refresh the tab; Focus on the tab; Open application tab; Refresh the session context; Set session context
OmnichannelLink record to the conversation; Unlink record from the conversation; Send knowledge base article link in chat (with the knowledge search action and Use an external portal = Yes). Needs Copilot Service workspace for Dynamics 365 Contact Center
FlowRun Flow and the Condition control

Session context. A case opened from Home is the anchor tab (the first tab); its columns become ${anchor.<column>}, and only the anchor tab fills the context. A conversation supplies ${customerName}, ${customerRecordId}, ${queueId} and ${LiveWorkItemId}. For a record in an additional tab, read ${Session.CurrentTab.entityId} and add an OData query.

Open a new form (3 attributes)  regardingobjectid     = ${anchor.incidentid}
                                regardingobjectidtype = incident
                                regardingobjectidname = ${anchor.title}
Autofill form fields (JSON)     regardingobjectid     = [{"id":"${anchor.incidentid}","name":"${anchor.title}","entitytype":"incident"}]
Update an existing record       regardingobjectid_incident@odata.bind = /incidents(${anchor.incidentid})
  • Autofill form fields does not save until the form autosaves: add Save the record (fails if mandatory fields are blank) or use Update an existing record.
  • Resolve a case needs Billable time, Incident ID and Resolution. Neither it nor Update an existing record refreshes the tab: add Get the current tab, then Refresh the tab with that Tab ID. After an update, add Refresh the session context so later slugs use the new value (the context is cached when the session starts).
  • Execute JavaScript needs a Web Resource Name and a Custom Macro Function, and links to non-Microsoft pages or applications. Open an email form with predefined template does not map Email recipients to the To field; follow it with Autofill form fields.
  • Run Flow lists instant cloud flows with the When a record is selected trigger; the rep needs a valid connection and permission to run the flow.
  • Troubleshoot: Productivity > Scripts > the script > the Macro step > Target macro > View history; each record is a run, and a failed run shows the failing step. Runs are logged in the Macro Run History (msdyn_macrosession) table. In the browser console, Microsoft.Apm.getFocusedSession().resolveSlug(...) tests a slug written without the $.
Exam traps: macros
  • Every macro begins with Start macro execution.
  • Only the anchor tab fills the session context, so columns of a record in an additional tab are not available as slugs.
  • Run Flow returns no output parameter and the rep signs in to the flow on every run, so a flow's result cannot feed later actions.
  • Refresh the session context reloads cached slug values; it does not redraw a stale tab (Refresh the tab does).
  • Omnichannel actions appear only with Copilot Service workspace for Contact Center, and switching conversations mid-run can give unexpected results.

Sources: Manage scripts · Scripts for reps · Automation dictionary · Macros · Productivity automation · Session connector · Omnichannel connector · Flow connector · Run history · Experience profile

sections.title: 2.3 Configure the Copilot Service workspace
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure session templates • create experience profiles • configure the Inbox, including creating custom views • configure application tab templates. Build one generic session template with an anchor tab, one custom experience profile mapped to a role, one multi-entity inbox view and one third-party-website application tab, then accept a conversation as a rep and watch the session open.

Names you will meet

The app is Copilot Service workspace and its admin app is Copilot Service admin center (older pages say Customer Service workspace and admin center). The docs now call a human agent a customer service representative (rep). The three out-of-the-box profiles keep the old wording. All four topics live under Support experience > Workspaces.

Configure session templates

A session template is a reusable bundle that decides what a rep gets when a session starts: the anchor tab (opens first, can't be closed), any additional tabs, and the default communication panel mode. Reps can work in up to nine sessions with up to 10 tabs each. Create one with Workspaces > Manage (Session templates) > New.

General tab fieldRule
Name vs TitleName is not visible to reps; Title is (for example {customerName}). Apply session title to anchor tab copies it to the anchor tab.
Unique Name<prefix>_<name>: alphanumeric prefix of 3–8 characters, then an underscore. The light bulb > Apply validates it. Application tab templates use the same rule.
TypeEntity shows an Entity field (user-owned tables only). Generic is for any channel.
Anchor tabDisplayed only when Type = Generic; the chosen application opens by default and can't be closed.
Communication panel modeDocked (expanded), Minimized or Hidden. A case (entity routing) session always has the panel hidden.
Session IconGeneric only; needs a deployed web resource file (no slugs); GIF isn't supported.
NeedUse
Session for a record such as a caseEntity template with Entity = Case (out of the box: Case entity session - default template)
Session for a channel conversationGeneric template with Anchor tab = Active Conversation
More tabs opened with the sessionAdditional Tab > Add Existing Application Tab Template (the docs say reps can't close them)
Default script for this templateScripts tab > Enable build expression = Yes (§2.2)
  1. Create the application tab templates the session needs.
  2. Create the session template and save it.
  3. Add the additional tabs and the optional script expression, then save.
  4. Associate it: workstream > Advanced settings > Sessions > Edit > Default template (§2.1). Entity templates are linked from an experience profile with Add entity session template.

Out-of-the-box templates (Case entity session - default template plus generic ones such as Chat session - default, Voice call session - default, SMS session - default and WhatsApp session - default) can't be customized; create your own. Loading generic templates with the createsession API requires the Channel Integration Framework to be enabled.

Exam traps
  • No Anchor tab field means Type is Entity; switch to Generic.
  • Editing an out-of-the-box template isn't possible; create a custom one.
  • A saved template does nothing until it is associated with a workstream or, for entity templates, a profile.
  • For a case session, expecting a docked panel is wrong: the panel stays hidden.
  • Notification templates alert reps to incoming work; session templates shape the session itself.

Create experience profiles

Experience profiles give reps and supervisors targeted experiences in Copilot Service workspace and are an alternative to building and maintaining custom apps. A profile bundles session templates, conversation channels, productivity tools and the inbox. The three out-of-the-box profiles (Omnichannel for Customer Service, Customer Service workspace and Customer Service workspace + channels, each with "- default profile") can't be deleted or modified, set as default, or given roles or a rank. A user with no custom profile gets the out-of-the-box default.

RoleWhat it means here
App Profile Manager Administrator + Basic UserPrerequisites to create profiles in the admin center. Give the first role manually to whoever creates profiles, templates, productivity tools and channel provider configurations.
Customer Service Representative, CSR ManagerInclude the App Profile User privileges (read access) out of the box, not the manager role.
Omnichannel administratorAlready includes the App Profile Manager Administrator privileges.
  1. Experience profiles > New: Name, Unique name (<prefix>_<name>), Description > Create.
  2. Open the profile: Users > Add Users; Add entity session template; Productivity pane On with a default mode (expanded or collapsed) and the tools Copilot, Knowledge search, Agent scripts, Join a Teams call, Teams chats, Smart assist, Case handling time, Screen Recording, Timeout Rules; Inbox > Edit; Channel providers > Edit (All active channels, third-party voice providers).
  3. Assign the profile as below.

Copilot features are available in the out-of-the-box profiles by default; in a custom profile you enable them yourself.

MethodSet withRules
DefaultSet as defaultOnly one default; use Remove Default first to switch. It doesn't apply to users who have a specific profile or role mapping. Making a profile default removes its roles and blocks new role mappings.
Role-basedSet rank and roles (Rank, Roles)Everyone holding the role gets the profile. With several mapped roles the higher rank wins (rank 1 over 2). Team membership isn't allowed.
DirectProfile > Users > Add UsersNamed users. Search by user shows which method applies to someone.

Rollout order: create users, assign security roles, build workstreams, queues, sessions and productivity tools, create profiles, then assign them (an existing organization needs only the last two).

Exam traps
  • Out-of-the-box profiles are read-only and can never be the default.
  • CSR and CSR Manager roles include the read-level App Profile User privileges, not the manager role, so the person creating profiles needs App Profile Manager Administrator and Basic User.
  • Security roles map profiles; teams don't. Rank 1 outranks rank 2.
  • A profile set as default loses its roles and can't take new ones.
  • "App profile" and "experience profile" name the same thing.

Configure the Inbox, including creating custom views

The inbox lists the cases, conversations and records assigned to a rep, and an inbox item can be promoted to a regular session. It is configurable for custom experiences only, so work in a custom profile. Supported: live chat, asynchronous chat, case (Customer Service only), email, task, voice and unified-routing records; the asynchronous channels are SMS, persistent chat, Facebook, WeChat, LINE, WhatsApp and Teams. Prerequisite: the profile's Channel providers must have All active channels On to configure chat settings.

  1. Open the custom profile (Experience profiles > Manage); on the Inbox card select Edit.
  2. Turn Enable Inbox On, then select + Add (Add a new view).
  3. Enter Name, Representative visibility (Show or Hide) and the Record types (several allowed = a multi-entity view).
  4. For each record type choose Simple (presets) or Advanced (condition builder), then Save.
Record typeSimple presets
CaseAssigned to me • in my team(s) • in my queue(s)
EmailSent to me • assigned to me • in my team(s) • in my queue(s) • in a shared mailbox
Chat, VoicemailAssigned • Unassigned • Resolved
Unified routing recordsAssigned • Open • Closed
  • Custom sort: Edit view pane > Sort (entity, attributes, order beyond customer and date). Bring your own entity: Inbox settings > Inbox record types tab > +Add. Custom card configuration: same tab, select an attribute to rearrange or add fields.
  • Channel-focused inbox: Edit inbox > Incoming work items tab, then choose: add to the inbox if the rep is in it (otherwise a new session tab), always add to the inbox, or always open a new session tab. Save, then clear the cache or refresh. It applies organization-wide, to all profiles and all conversation types except voice, which always opens a new session with a card in the inbox.
  • Views refresh automatically every five minutes; by default they show work from the last 90 days (Modified On) and the top 500 records. The two inbox articles list different out-of-the-box view names, so learn the mechanism rather than the names.
Exam traps
  • Out-of-the-box profiles can't hold inbox changes; build a custom profile first.
  • Configuring chat settings requires All active channels to be On.
  • One view can mix record types; you don't need one view per type, and Simple or Advanced is chosen per record type.
  • Hide keeps a view away from reps; Show makes it visible.
  • The channel-focused setting is not per profile, and voice never follows it.

Configure application tab templates

An application tab template says which application opens in a tab when a session starts (for example Active Conversation). It applies to Customer Service and Contact Center—standalone only. Every session has at least one anchor tab, and the Home session can't be closed or customized. The article lists System Administrator as the prerequisite (App Profile Manager Administrator also holds the table privileges). Out-of-the-box templates can't be customized.

  1. Workspaces > Manage (Application tab templates) > New.
  2. General tab: Name (hidden from reps), Unique name, Title (shown), Page type, Description; Save.
  3. The Parameters section now lists the page type's parameters (save after every edit to refresh it); set each Value, then Save.
Page typeParameters (required in bold)Behaviour
DashboarddashboardIdBlank, wrong or not in the app module: default dashboard
Entity listentityName, viewIdMissing view: default view
Entity record (open)entityName, entityId, formId, validateRecordUnmatched entityId opens create mode unless validateRecord = True
Entity record (create)entityName, data (JSON), formIddata prefills the new form
SearchsearchText, searchType0 = Relevance, 1 = Categorized
Third-party websiteurl, dataNeeds an https:// URL; the site must allow iframe hosting
Web resourcewebresourceName, dataFor example new_myresource.html
Customname, entityName, recordIdA custom page's unique name

Control is for internal use only. Values accept slugs and OData. For a case opened as the anchor tab, both forms below give https://www.bing.com/search?q=CAS-01003-P3B7G1:

url  = https://www.bing.com/search?q=
data = {anchor.ticketnumber}
data = {$odata.incident.ticketnumber.?$filter=incidentid eq'{anchor.incidentid}'&$select=ticketnumber}

If validateRecord isn't listed, select New Template Parameter: Name validateRecord, Unique Name new_tabtemplateparam_validateRecord, Value True. Out-of-the-box templates: Active Conversation and Entity record (Entity record), Knowledge Search (Web resource), Omnichannel Conversations Dashboard (Dashboard), Omnichannel Intraday Insights, Quick Reply Preview and Rich Message Preview (Control), and Search (Control, Deprecated). Use a template as a session template's anchor or additional tab.

Exam traps
  • Web resource opens a file deployed in Dataverse (webresourceName); an external site is Third-party website (url).
  • The Search page type is the built-in entity search page (searchType 0 = Relevance, 1 = Categorized), not a search on an external site.
  • Without validateRecord = True, a wrong entityId opens a blank create form.
  • Third-party and web resource tabs reload to their initial state when the rep switches away and back (documented known issue).
  • Name is hidden from reps; Title is shown. Parameters appear only after the first Save.

Sources: Manage session templates · Overview of templates · Create and manage workstreams · Copilot Service workspace overview · Overview of experience profiles · Configure experience profiles · Add users to experience profiles · Roles and privileges for experience profiles · Configure the inbox · Inbox views and filters · Manage application tab templates
