sections.title: 3.1 Configure the data model and UI components
sections.html:
Skills measured: create and configure forms • create and configure views • configure model-driven app components • create and configure columns • configure alerts and in-app notifications • create or modify a table • configure relationships • configure Dataverse search • create and manage email templates. Practise in a trial environment by building one custom table end to end: columns, a lookup to Case, role-specific main forms, a quick create form, a public view, a Dataverse search entry and an email template with dynamic text.

Names in current docs
  • Maker articles say table, column, row and choice (older wording: entity, field, record, option set). The exam can use either set.
  • Customer Service articles now call the apps Copilot Service workspace and Copilot Service admin center (formerly Customer Service workspace and Customer Service admin center).

Create and configure forms

Forms are the pages people use to read and edit a row. Build them in the modern form designer; the classic app, form and view designers were deprecated from October 2023 and now open only in the modern designers. Customizing needs the System Administrator or System Customizer role. A table can have four form types:

TypeUse it forRules to remember
MainThe primary page of a row (tabs, sections, columns)Only type that supports tabs, security-role assignment, fallback status and the inactive state
Quick createFast entry in a side panel when a user selects Create in the navigation bar or + New in a lookup or subgridTable needs Enable quick create forms and must be in the app; always one section with three columns; no subgrids, quick view forms, web resources, iFrames, notes or Bing Maps; one form serves everyone (top of the form order). Case has one by default
Quick viewRead-only data from a related row, shown inside a main form by a quick view control tied to a lookup columnNeeds a lookup to that table (hidden when the lookup is empty); single-column tab; no header, footer, navigation, form scripts or custom controls; cannot be activated or deactivated
CardCompact display in views, subgrids and on small screens (timeline card forms are covered in §1.1)A custom card form in a view needs the deprecated Read-only Grid control

Create, edit and publish

  1. Power Apps → Solutions → open the solution → open the table → Forms area.
  2. New form → choose Main, Quick create, Quick view or Card, then enter a Form name and an optional description.
  3. Optional: Get AI generated column suggestions. Copilot proposes columns for quick view and quick create forms from the name and description; availability depends on region and Copilot settings.
  4. Select Create, then add columns from the Columns pane and components (subgrid, quick view, lookup, web resource and more) from the Components pane.
  5. Select Save and publish. Save only saves the form but users do not see the change until it is published. Save a copy clones a form. A new main form starts as a copy of an existing main form.

Who sees which form: Form settings

Open Form settings from the command bar in the Forms area or in the designer. It has four areas:

AreaWhat it does
Security roleChoose Everyone or Specific security roles for a main form. Quick create, quick view and card forms cannot be assigned to roles.
Form orderDrag forms within a set (Main, Quick Create, Quick View, Card). The top form is the default. Order does not decide who may open a form.
Fallback formsThe main form shown to users whose roles have no form assigned. At least one main form must be a fallback; fallback does not apply to the other form types.
Form access checkerVerifies which forms a user can access.
  • A table must keep at least one main form and one fallback form, so you cannot delete the only main form or the only fallback form. Create or designate another first.
  • A main form can be set inactive to stop anyone using it.
  • Typical strategies: one form for everyone; a minimal "contingency" form assigned only to System Administrator; or role-specific forms ranked above a generic fallback form at the bottom of the order.
  • By default an app shows all forms of an added table; restrict them in the app designer. In a managed solution you cannot edit forms unless the table's managed properties allow it.

Designer properties worth knowing

  • Form: Title (required), Description (makers only), Max Width (default 1900 px), Show image (shows the table's Primary Image in the header).
  • Tab: Label, Name (letters, digits and underscores; scripts use it), expanded by default, Hide, Hide on phone, up to three columns, column width 1–100. Tabs exist only on main forms.
  • Column: Label, Hide label, Hide, Lock (cannot be removed from the form), Read-only. A locked column, or a required column that is not elsewhere on the form, cannot be deleted from it.
  • Subgrid: pick Table, Default view, Show related records, Allow users to change view; Maximum number of rows is 2–250. It is a read-only list; use the editable grid for inline edits.
  • Creating a new table column from inside the form designer is labelled Preview on its article. Client scripts use formContext; Xrm.Page is Deprecated.
Exam traps
  • Form order is not security. Roles and fallback decide who can open a form; order only ranks the forms a user can already open.
  • Quick create, quick view and card forms cannot be assigned to security roles, and fallback exists for main forms only.
  • Hide and Read-only are form settings. The value is still reachable from other forms and the API, so use column-level security to protect data.
  • Quick create means one section with three columns and no subgrid, quick view, iFrame, web resource, notes or map. It also needs Enable quick create forms and the table in the app.
  • Quick view forms are read-only, need a lookup and cannot run scripts.
  • Save only does not publish; users keep seeing the old form.

Create and configure views

A view defines the columns shown, their order and width, the default sort and the default filters for a list of rows. There are three view types:

TypeOwnerRules to remember
PersonalOne person; private unless sharedCreated with Create view in the app; needs at least User-level access to the Saved View table; can be based on a system or public view, but a public or system view cannot be based on a personal view
SystemThe organization; edited by admins and customizersSpecial views the app depends on; not shown in the view selector; cannot be used in subgrids or dashboard lists; cannot be deleted or deactivated; they are cached, so plug-ins on savedquery are unsupported
PublicThe organizationAppears in the view selector; usable in subgrids and dashboard lists; custom public views can be deleted in an unmanaged solution; system-defined public views cannot
System viewPurpose
Quick FindDefault view for Quick Find searches. Its Find columns decide which columns are searched, and it also drives Dataverse search (see the Dataverse search topic below).
Advanced FindDefault view for Advanced Find results; supplies the default columns for new views created without a template.
AssociatedLists the related rows of a record.
LookupShown when a user picks a row for a lookup column.

A new custom table receives Active and Inactive public views plus one Quick Find, Advanced Find, Associated and Lookup system view.

Build and publish a public view

  1. Power Apps → Solutions → open the solution → open the table → Views area. In the app designer you can instead select a table page and choose Edit view.
  2. Select Add view, enter a name and description, then Create.
  3. Add columns with + View column or drag them from Table columns. Use the column header menu for Filter by, sorting and Move Left/Right, and drag to resize.
  4. Sort with Sort by and then Then sort by. For complex filters choose Edit filters (expression builder: Add row, Add group, Add related table; And is the default).
  5. Select Save and publish. Makers choose which public views an app exposes in the app designer.
  6. To make it the landing view: ... next to a public view → Set as default view. A user's own pinned personal default wins over it.
  • In a related-table filter, Contains data is the only operator allowed. Public views built in Power Apps that use Contains data or Does not contain data do not appear in the Advanced Find saved-views list.
  • Grid controls: the Power Apps grid control (read-only or editable) is the current one; the Power Apps read-only grid, Editable grid and legacy Read-only grid are all labelled Deprecated.
  • Role-based access to system views: set the organization setting EnableRoleBasedSystemViews to true (OrganizationSettingsEditor tool), be a System Administrator, then on a non-default public view choose View settings → Specific security roles → Save and publish. It only filters the table's view selector (subgrids still list all views, and users can still reach every view through Manage and share views) and it does not secure data. The Views overview article labels this feature as preview while its own article carries no label, so confirm the status before relying on it.
  • Public views in Customer Service examples: All Cases, Cases I follow, My Cases, My Resolved cases.
Exam traps
  • System views (Quick Find, Advanced Find, Associated, Lookup) are not selectable in the view selector and cannot feed a subgrid or dashboard. Build a public view for that.
  • The table's default view is chosen from the public views; a personal view is owned by one person.
  • Editing a public view does not change what search matches; the Quick Find view does.
  • Role-based view access filters only the table view selector and does not protect data.
  • For related-table filters only Contains data is offered.

Configure model-driven app components

A model-driven app is built from components grouped by purpose. Know the category and the designer that owns each one:

CategoryComponentsDesigner
DataTable, relationship, column, choice columnTable designer
UIApp, site map, form, view, custom pageApp, form and view designers; Power Apps Studio for custom pages
LogicBusiness process flow, workflow, action, business rule, Power Automate flowThe designer for each process type
VisualizationChart, dashboard, embedded Power BIChart and dashboard designers

Modern app designer

  • Add page types: Dataverse table (adds a view page and a form page), Dashboard (system, interactive or Power BI), Custom page, Web resource, Navigation link; "Describe a page" creates an AI-generated page and is labelled Preview. Clear Show in navigation to keep a page out of the site map.
  • Settings: General (Solution is read-only, App name, Description, Icon), Advanced (Unique name, Welcome page, Primary mobile player) and Features (for example In app notifications). Changes take effect only after Publish.

Dashboards, processes and commands

  • Dashboards: a system dashboard (admin-made, visible to all) or a user dashboard (private); standard or interactive experience (Unified Interface only). Layouts: 2-column overview, 3-column overview, 3-column overview (varied width), 4-column overview, Power BI embedded. A dashboard holds up to six charts or lists; the Add Component dialog asks for Record Type, View and Chart. Adding the Customer Service Manager dashboard brings in the Case, Entitlement and Queue Item tables, and an app with no dashboards selected shows all of them. Both statements come from the classic app designer tutorial; the current app designer articles don't repeat them.
  • Business process flows: stages contain steps (each step is a column); required steps give stage-gating. Limits: up to 5 tables per flow, 10 active flows per table, 30 stages; only one flow renders on form load.
  • Command designer: a command has display, action and visibility settings. Locations: Main grid, Main form, Subgrid view, Associated view (plus quick actions tied to the main grid). Types: Command, Dropdown, Group, Split button.
  • Copilot Service workspace is itself a model-driven app. Representatives can open up to nine sessions with up to ten tabs each, and the Copilot Service workspace overview says multisession navigation is supported in that app only, not in a custom app or a copy of it. A separate Learn article describes enabling the multisession experience in a custom model-driven app (not in default apps such as Sales Hub), so the pages disagree; treat the workspace overview as the stricter statement (§2.3 covers its templates and profiles).
  • Custom pages are generally available: the custom page overview lists runtime, authoring and solution (ALM) support as General Availability, and only custom pages in a Teams model-driven app and in mobile online are in public preview. The component overview article still shows an older Preview label.
Exam traps
  • A dashboard canvas holds six components at most; interactive dashboards appear only in Unified Interface.
  • The classic app designer tutorial says adding a dashboard or a business process flow automatically adds the tables it uses; the current app designer articles don't state this.
  • App-level switches such as In app notifications live in Settings → Features and need Publish.

Create and configure columns

Create columns in the table designer: Tables → open the table → Columns → New column, then set Display Name, Name, Data type, Format, Behavior, Required and Searchable. Nothing is created until you Save Table.

Data typeFacts
Text, Text AreaDefault 100, maximum 4,000 characters; lowering the maximum does not truncate existing data
Multiline TextDefault 150, maximum 1,048,576 characters
Decimal / Floating PointDecimal is exact with up to 10 precision points; floating point is an approximation with up to 5
CurrencyAdds a Currency lookup, an Exchange Rate and a _Base column; precision options: Pricing Decimal Precision, Currency Precision, or 0–4
Date and Time / Date OnlyBehaviors: User local (default), Date only, Time zone independent
Choice / ChoicesSingle or multi-select; local options or a shared global choice
LookupCreates an N:1 relationship; types Simple, Customer, Owner, PartyList (system only), Regarding
ImageOne per table, always named tableImage; under 30 MB; stored outside the relational store
AutonumberString prefixed, date prefixed or custom format; default seed 1000; gaps can appear

Choosing a behavior

NeedUseKey facts
Value from the same row or related parent rows, immediatelyCalculatedCondition and Action editor; creating one needs Write on the Field Security Profile table; column security on the related table is ignored, so secure the calculated column too
Power Fx expression evaluated when rows are readFormula (a data type)Decimal precision 0–10, default 2; the article has no preview label, but "Get formula suggestions" is labelled preview
Aggregate over related child rows or a hierarchyRollupSUM, COUNT, MIN, MAX, AVG with filters. Calculated by asynchronous system jobs: Mass Calculate Rollup Field runs 12 hours after you create or edit the column; Calculate Rollup Field is incremental with a default minimum recurrence of one hour. Creates _date and _state helper columns
Plain stored valueSimple (default)
  • Required levels: Optional, Business Recommended, Business Required. A required column on a hidden tab or section does not block saving unless it also appears in a visible one. Only SystemRequired is enforced for programmatic saves. Use business rules to change requirement dynamically.
  • Searchable makes a column available in Advanced Find and when customizing views. It does not add it to Dataverse search.
  • Choices (multi-select) cannot be used with workflows, business process flows, actions, business rules, charts, rollup or calculated columns, or reports, and in Customer Service tables not with SLAs (§1.5) or routing rules (§2.1). They can use global choices.
  • After you save a column, its Name (publisher prefix included) and Data type are locked; the Create and edit columns article lists one exception, converting a Text column to Autonumber. The display name can still change.
  • A lookup stores the target's primary name, which anyone who can read the row can see, so keep sensitive text out of primary name columns.

Secure a column (ordered)

  1. Open the column → Advanced options → select Enable column security → Save. This needs the System Administrator role.
  2. Power Platform admin center → Manage → Environments → your environment → Settings → Users + permissions → Column security profiles.
  3. Create or open a profile, add the Teams or Users, then on the Column Permission tab set Read, Read unmasked, Update and Create for the column.

Without a profile only System Administrators can use a secured column; others see masked asterisks. System Administrators are never blocked, so test with another account.

Exam traps
  • A calculated column cannot aggregate child rows; use a rollup, which refreshes on a schedule rather than instantly.
  • Multi-select Choices fail in business rules, rollup and calculated columns, and in Customer Service SLAs and routing rules.
  • Hide and Read-only on a form do not secure data; column security profiles do, and they do not apply to System Administrators.
  • Searchable is not the Dataverse search setting (that is the Quick Find view).
  • Column Name and Data type cannot be edited after saving; plan names and types first.
  • Decimal is exact; floating point is an approximation.

Configure alerts and in-app notifications

The skill title says "alerts", but the documentation uses that word for several different things. The reading that is documented as a configuration task from start to finish is in-app notifications, so treat it as the core; recognise the others.

ReadingWhere you configure itNotes
In-app notifications (platform)App designer → Settings → Features; send with the SendAppNotification messagePer user; notification center plus toast
Notification templates for representativesCopilot Service admin center → Support experience → Workspaces → NotificationsTwo kinds: toast notifications (float and disappear) and alert notifications (dialog with buttons)
Customer Voice alertsProject → Reports → Alerts (see §3.2)Rules on satisfaction metrics create follow-up alerts
Client API messagesForm scriptssetFormNotification (ERROR, WARNING, INFO), Xrm.Navigation.openAlertDialog, Xrm.App.addGlobalNotification (levels 1 Success, 2 Error, 3 Warning, 4 Information)

In-app notifications

  1. Power Apps → open the solution → select the app → Edit (modern app designer).
  2. Settings → Features → turn on In-app notifications (the app-settings article spells it "In app notifications").
  3. Save, then Publish the app.
  4. Send notifications with SendAppNotification; they are stored in the Notification (appnotification) table.
ParameterValues and notes
RecipientOne user (for example /systemusers(GUID)). Teams are not supported; create one notification per user.
Title, BodyPlain text; use OverrideContent for a limited markdown subset (bold, italic, lists, links)
ToastTypeTimed 200000000 (default, about four seconds) or Hidden 200000001 (notification center only)
IconTypeInfo (default), Success, Failure, Warning (100000003, used below), Mention or Custom (needs iconUrl)
PriorityNormal 200000000 (default) or High 200000001; High sorts to the top of the notification center
TTLInSeconds, DataExpiry in seconds (default lifetime is 14 days); JSON up to 5,000 characters
ActionsZero or more: URL, Side Pane, Teams Chat. A URL in an unsupported format is blocked, so the notification shows but the action does nothing
POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/SendAppNotification
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{
  "Title": "SLA critical",
  "Body": "Record assigned to you is critically past SLA.",
  "Recipient": "/systemusers(<GUID of the user>)",
  "IconType": 100000003,
  "ToastType": 200000000
}
  • The app polls for notifications when it starts and on page navigation if the last check was more than a minute ago, so delivery is not instant.
  • @mentions in notes trigger notifications; @mentions in timeline posts do not.
  • To call SendAppNotification a user needs the Send In-App Notification privilege (prvSendAppNotification, Miscellaneous privileges tab), which the Environment Maker role has by default. Receiving needs Read on the notification table plus rights on the app user setting. Notifications use Dataverse storage.
  • Users can switch toasts on or off and set their duration from the bell → Settings. In-app notifications are separate from push notifications: the Power Apps Notification connector sends push notifications to the Power Apps, Field Service or Sales mobile app, and recipients must have that app installed, be signed in and allow notifications in the mobile OS.

Notification templates for representatives

  • Path: Copilot Service admin center → Support experience → Workspaces → Manage for Notifications → Templates tab → New Notification Template.
  • General fields: Name, Title, Icon, Show Countdown, Countdown (seconds), Accept Button, Reject Button, Show desktop notifications (default Never; When app is in background; Always Preview), plus Autoassign work items and Autoaccept voice/chat calls (both Preview). Then add notification fields: a Field header and a slug Value such as {customerName} or {caseTitle}.
  • Out-of-the-box templates cannot be edited; create your own. When unified routing assigns a record and notifications are on, the assignee sees a case-assignment notification and cannot reject it (§2.1).
Exam traps
  • In-app notifications are per user; a team recipient is not supported, so loop over the members.
  • The feature must be switched on per app (Settings → Features) and the app republished.
  • Do not confuse in-app notifications, push notifications and Copilot Service workspace notification templates.
  • Priority only orders the notification center; it does not widen the audience.
  • Rep notification templates cannot be edited when they ship with the product, and a record-routing assignment cannot be rejected.

Create or modify a table

You need the System Customizer role plus a role with Create, Read and Write on the Entity table. Make tables in Power Apps: Tables → New table. The list tabs are Recommended (standard tables), Custom and All. Paths: Create new tables (data workspace: Start with Copilot, import a SharePoint list, import Excel or CSV, or start from blank), Set advanced properties, Create with external data (only the first 20 rows preview), or Create a virtual table. The data workspace cannot create Rich text, Customer, Autonumber or Formula columns, and does not support many-to-many relationships.

Table typeUse it for
StandardNormal business data (account, contact, user and your custom tables)
ActivityTask-like rows with start, due and duration (appointment, email, fax, letter, phone call, recurring appointment, task); only a user or team can own; primary field is Subject
VirtualData that stays in an external source
ElasticVery large datasets (tens of millions of rows), powered by Azure Cosmos DB
OwnershipMeaning
User or teamActions on rows can be controlled per user
OrganizationAccess is controlled at organization level
Filtered PreviewAccess by filter privileges on a column value; rows have no owner, so they cannot be assigned or shared

Advanced options you may be asked about (exact labels): Apply duplicate detection rules, Track changes, Audit changes to its data, Leverage quick create form if available, Enable long term retention, Creating a new activity, Can have connections, Can have a contact email, Have an access team, Can be linked to feedback, Appear in search results and Can be added to a queue. Also Enable Attachments for notes and files.

  • Irreversible after save: ownership type, schema name (publisher prefix, no spaces), the primary column's display name and description, and Creating a new activity (once enabled it cannot be disabled).
  • For Customer Service: Can be added to a queue lets a table work with queues (§2.1); Track changes plus Appear in search results are required for Dataverse search; Enable quick create forms backs the quick create form.
Exam traps
  • Ownership cannot be changed later: a wrongly owned custom table must be deleted and recreated.
  • Activity tables cannot be organization-owned.
  • "Creating a new activity" is a one-way switch.
  • Dataverse search needs both Track changes and Appear in search results.
  • Filtered ownership is a preview option; elastic tables are for very large volumes, not general use.

Configure relationships

Dataverse has only two relationship types: 1:N and N:N. N:1 is the same 1:N relationship seen from the child table, and adding a lookup column creates a 1:N relationship. A N:N relationship uses a special relationship (intersect) table so rows on both sides can have many partners.

  1. Power Apps → Solutions → open the table → Relationships area → New relationship → Many-to-one, One-to-many or Many-to-many.
  2. Pick the Related table. Set the lookup display name and name, Lookup column requirement (Optional, Business Recommended, Business Required), Searchable and the relationship name.
  3. Expand Advanced options for relationship behavior and navigation display, then select Done and Save table.

The lookup column always lives on the "many" (child) table: for one-to-many it is created on the related table, for many-to-one on the current table. If you create two N:N relationships between the same tables, make the relationship name and relationship table name unique.

Standard behaviorWhat happens
Referential, Remove LinkRows are navigable but actions do not cascade; deleting the parent just clears the lookup on children
Referential, Restrict DeleteParent cannot be deleted while related child rows exist
ParentalAny action on the parent (assign, share, delete and so on) is also applied to the child rows
CustomYou pick an option for each action
ActionOptions
Assign, Reparent, Share, UnshareCascade All, Cascade Active, Cascade User-owned, Cascade None
DeleteCascade All, Remove Link, Restrict
MergeCascade All, Cascade None
Rollup ViewCascade All, Cascade Active, Cascade User-owned, Cascade None
  • Cascade Active acts on active child rows only; Cascade User-owned acts on child rows owned by the same user as the parent row; Restrict blocks deleting the parent.
  • Cascading limits: a custom table cannot be the primary table in a cascading relationship with a related system table, and a related table cannot be the child in two cascading relationships.
  • Lookup types: Simple, Customer (account or contact, which gives two parental relationships), Owner, PartyList (system-created), Regarding (activities). Custom multi-table lookups cannot be created in the maker portal.
  • Hierarchy: a self-referential 1:N can be marked Hierarchical = Yes, once per table; this enables the Under and Not Under operators. Disabling or changing it breaks rollups, views and processes that depend on it.
  • Connections (connection roles) are the informal alternative for loose links such as "friend of"; relationships are formal metadata used by queries and reports.
Exam traps
  • N:1 is not a third type, and the lookup sits on the child (many) side.
  • Parental cascades every action; when you need only some, use Custom (for example Delete = Cascade All and Assign = Cascade User-owned).
  • Restrict Delete blocks the parent delete; Remove Link lets it proceed and clears the lookup.
  • A custom table cannot be the parent of a cascading relationship to a system table.
  • Only one hierarchical relationship per table; do not toggle it casually.

Configure Dataverse search

Dataverse search returns relevance-ranked results from many tables in one list, tolerates typos, respects security roles and also searches documents, notes and attachments (2 MB file limit). It is an opt-out feature and cannot be turned off for a single app.

Turn it on or off (admin)

  1. Power Platform admin center → Manage → Environments → select the environment (System Administrator).
  2. Settings → expand Product → Features → Dataverse search.
  3. Choose the options: Turn on search indexing to support Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) in AI and agent experiences and/or Show global search bar in all model-driven apps and turn on search indexing to support search-only experiences; Save.
  • With global search on, the multi-table Quick Find ("categorized search") is unavailable. Turning Dataverse search off removes the index within 12 hours; turning it on again needs a full sync (an hour or more, days for large organizations).

Choose tables and fields

  1. Table is customizable, in the app, and has Track changes and Appear in search results turned on in Advanced options.
  2. Power Apps → Solutions → choose the solution → Edit → Overview → Dataverse search pane → Manage search index; select the tables.
  3. Open the table → Data experiences → Views → the Quick Find view; edit Find, View and Filter columns; Save and publish. Confirm the Quick Find view is the table's default view.
  • Find columns = searchable fields (only text, lookup and choice columns count; other types are ignored). View columns = what the results show. Filter columns/conditions apply to results; operators such as Like, BeginsWith, Null and NotNull are unsupported. The first four facetable View columns become the facets. Related-table fields are ignored.
  • Limits: 50 fields indexed by default, 1,000 per organization (so 950 configurable); a lookup counts as 3 fields, a state or status choice as 2, other types as 1. No limit on the number of tables. Search terms are limited to 1,024 characters; configuration changes can take up to 15 minutes to reach the service.
  • Knowledge Article is indexed by default, and so are Case, Service and Service Activity when Dynamics 365 apps are allowed; custom tables must be added. To let representatives search chat transcripts, configure the Note table for Dataverse search and add it to the app (§1.2 covers knowledge search).
Dataverse searchQuick FindAdvanced Find
ScopeMany tables, one relevance-ranked list; no table maximumOne table, or multi-table (categorized) up to 10 tablesOne table, query builder
MatchingAny word, any column; trailing wildcardAll words in one column; leading wildcardCriteria you define
ColumnsText, lookup, choice onlyAll searchable columnsAll searchable columns
Exam traps
  • The Quick Find view drives Dataverse search; the column Searchable property only affects Advanced Find and view customization.
  • Numeric and date Find columns are ignored by Dataverse search.
  • A custom table needs Track changes and Appear in search results, and has to be added to the index and the app.
  • You cannot switch Dataverse search off for one app; turning it off drops the index within 12 hours.
  • Limits: 50 default fields, 1,000 maximum (950 configurable).

Create and manage email templates

Email templates give agents consistent, preformatted messages.

  1. In the Email Templates area select New → Start with a blank template or Start with existing templates.
  2. Enter Template name, Permission level (Organization = everyone can use it; Individual = personal, visible only to the owner or people it is shared with), Category (default User) and Language.
  3. Select Create. The editor has Designer, HTML, Template (details and subject) and Attachments tabs and accepts up to 1,048,576 characters.

The Category decides which record types and fields Insert dynamic text offers. The enhanced email template editor, the legacy rich text editor and drag-and-drop were removed on May 23, 2025; templates open in the modern rich text editor (HTML formatting).

Field typeDynamic text syntax
Text, currency, multiline, decimal, floating{!EntityLogicalName:FieldLogicalName;}
Lookup, choice, multi-select choice{!EntityLogicalName:FieldLogicalName/@name;}
Date{!EntityLogicalName:FieldLogicalName/@date;}
Time{!EntityLogicalName:FieldLogicalName/@time;}

Example from the docs: Dear {!User:First Name;}. Dynamic text in a hyperlink or anchor tag is not supported.

  • Insert Template filters by the email's fields: with a Recipient (TO) you see user (global) and contact templates; with a Regarding row you see user (global) and that table's templates. The admin setting Skip Select Record dialog hides the intermediary dialog. The enhanced selection dialog is enabled by adding the Enable the New Insert Template Dialog setting to a solution (not the default solution) and setting its environment value to Yes; an app can override it.
  • Manage for representatives: Copilot Service admin center → Support experience → Productivity → Manage for Email templates.
  • Copilot prompts in a template: you need the CSR Manager and System Administrator roles and the setting that lets Copilot recommend email templates under Copilot for questions and emails (the checkbox is worded "Copilot recommended email templates" on one article and "Copilot for email templates" on another). Open the template → Insert Copilot prompts → write one or more prompts → add alternate text for representatives who cannot use Copilot → optionally turn on Use knowledge sources (only one prompt per template can use them) → Submit → Save.
  • Line of business: add the Line of Business (Multi Select) column to the Email Template form, add matching values to the LOB Category choice (names must match the Customer Intent Agent), then tag templates. Copilot picks the template for the case's line of business, or drafts without a template if none matches.
  • Queue signature: Copilot Service admin center → Customer support → Queues → Manage Basic queues → queue → Email Signature. If none is set, the queue owner's signature is used.
  • Customer Voice has its own survey email templates (§3.2); they are separate from these.
Exam traps
  • Individual templates are invisible to others unless shared; Organization templates are for everyone.
  • The template Category controls available dynamic text fields; it does not control who sees the template.
  • Dynamic text inside a hyperlink does not work, and lookup or choice fields need the /@name; suffix.
  • Copilot knowledge sources work for only one prompt per template, and the alternate text is what users without Copilot see.
  • The enhanced email template editor and drag-and-drop no longer exist.

Sources: Create and edit forms · Control access to forms · Quick create forms · Quick view forms · Views overview · Default view · Manage view access · App components · App designer · Custom pages overview · Column data types · Rollup columns · Column-level security · Send in-app notifications · Notification templates · Create and edit tables · Types of tables · Table relationships · Configure Dataverse search · Create an email template · Dynamic text · Copilot prompts in templates

sections.title: 3.2 Capture customer feedback by using Customer Voice
sections.html:
Skills measured: trigger distribution of a survey • personalize a survey • populate survey results against cases and conversations. Practise in a trial environment: create a project from the Support template, check that its case-resolved flow is on, add a variable to a question, resolve a test case and open the response from the case timeline.

Trigger distribution of a survey

Dynamics 365 Customer Voice (built on Microsoft Forms, formerly Microsoft Forms Pro) keeps surveys in a project: a container for surveys, satisfaction metrics, email templates, Power Automate flows and reports. Project templates are Periodic customer feedback, Order delivery, Service visit, Support (case management) and Blank.

  • Where data lives: invitations and responses are stored in the Dataverse environment you pick when you create the project. The Customer Voice app must be installed in that environment (Sales, Customer Service, Marketing and Talent organizations already have the tables) and makers need the Project Owner role.
  • Licensing: included with select Dynamics 365 enterprise products with 2,000 responses per month tenant-wide; extra responses are sold in bundles. Otherwise buy the Customer Voice license plus the free user subscription license for each user.
Method (Send tab)Use whenKey facts
EmailAd hoc send to a listBuilt-in composer; default sender surveys@email.formspro.microsoft.com; 10,000 emails a day on the default domain, 50,000 with a custom domain; up to 10,000 recipients and 10,000 contacts per CSV import; unsubscribe link added by default; up to 10 saved email templates
Power AutomateA business event should send itFive out-of-the-box templates: case resolved, lead qualified, order fulfilled, Power Apps button click, work order completed or closed; connector actions Send a survey and Create an invitation only (it has no triggers)
EmbedOn a web pageInline, Pop-up window or Button; Only people in my organization can respond must be off
Link / QR codePosters, receipts, chatsNon-personalized, so responses are always anonymous and variables are not replaced
Send Survey commandA rep sends from a recordNeeds the Send survey app, a configured flow and the Survey Sender role (below)
Post-conversation surveyAfter a chat, SMS or social conversationWorkstream setting in Copilot Service admin center (below)

Survey automatically when a case is resolved (ordered)

  1. Prerequisite: Dynamics 365 Customer Service is in the same tenant.
  2. Create a project from the Support template and edit or customize the survey.
  3. On the Send tab select Automation and choose Send a survey when a case is resolved in Dynamics 365.
  4. Verify the connection details, select Continue, then Create.
  5. Confirm in Power Automate (My flows) that the flow is on; flows created from a project template start in the inactive state.
  6. Resolve a case in Customer Service. The survey goes to the contact or account linked to the case.

In the Send a survey action, Regarding takes the table's logical name (for Case: incident) and only tables marked for collaboration in activities are supported (Task is not); Recipient details takes a Contact only. To deliver by Outlook, Gmail or SMS instead, use Create an invitation: it returns InviteId, InviteUrl and UnsubscribeUrl; the invitation cannot be edited, and invites save to Dataverse asynchronously, so add a delay before using them.

Send Survey from a Dynamics 365 record

  • Administrator installs the Send Customer Voice survey from Dynamics 365 app, then in that solution sets the connection references and turns on the flow Send survey on create of custom entity record.
  • Users need at least the Survey Sender role and can send only surveys they created or that were shared with them (sharing needs Share privilege on the Customer Voice survey table).
  • Available from Contact, Opportunity, Lead, Account, Case and Contract: open the record → Send Survey → pick one survey → Next → Recipient, Email template, Locale (variables appear as fields) → Send. Check status (Sending, Sent, Failed) with Advanced Find → Customer Voice Send survey history → Status Reason.

Post-conversation survey (ordered)

  1. Create the survey in Customer Voice in the same organization as the contact center.
  2. Copilot Service admin center → Customer support → Workstreams → open the channel instance → Edit.
  3. Behaviors tab → set Post-conversation survey to On and choose the Dynamics 365 Customer Voice survey.
  4. Under How should we send the survey pick Send survey link to conversation, or Insert survey in conversation (Live chat only; the representative inserts it so questions show in the chat window).
  5. Optional: tick Bot conversation survey for AI-agent conversations (it can reuse the same settings), then Save and close.

Supported channels: Live chat, SMS (Twilio), Facebook, LINE, WhatsApp, custom channel and Microsoft Teams. The post-conversation survey article still also lists SMS (TeleSign) and Apple Messages for Business, but the TeleSign SMS channel was removed on October 8, 2024, and Apple Messages for Business was deprecated on July 17, 2026, with removal from Copilot Service admin center scheduled for September 30, 2026. Post-conversation surveys are not supported in Government Community Cloud.

Distribution settings and sender

GroupSettings (defaults)
ParticipantsOnly people in my organization can respond (off; sign-in required when on); Anonymous responses (off); One response per person (off); Save invited participants as Contacts (on); Save survey progress (off)
ResponsesAccept responses (on); start and end date; Response limit (maximum 50,000)
AvailabilityDisable survey links after N days (default 30, maximum 1,095)
Email and NotificationsSender list; confirmation email to respondents; email to you on each submission
  • Custom sender address: a tenant administrator uses Microsoft 365 admin center → Settings → Org settings → Services → Dynamics 365 Customer Voice → Distribution tab → + Add domain, creates the DNS records, verifies, then adds the address, display name and approved users. Not available in Government Community Cloud. The Security tab holds Prevent phishing attempts and Collect names (both on by default).
  • Newer option: in Copilot Service admin center, Customer support → Customer settings → Customer feedback → Manage → New creates a Copilot Studio survey agent from CSAT, NPS, Customer Effort Score or Blank templates. The voice workstream post-call survey toggle (Language tab) was removed effective August 1, 2025 Deprecated; Microsoft points to these survey agents instead.
Exam traps
  • Regarding needs the table's logical name (incident, not "Case"); Task is not supported; Recipient details accepts a Contact only.
  • Flows made from project templates are created inactive; nothing is sent until you turn them on.
  • Generic links, QR codes and embedded surveys are non-personalized, so responses are anonymous; embedding fails if "Only people in my organization" is on.
  • Insert survey in conversation works only for Live chat; post-conversation surveys and custom senders are not available in GCC.
  • Default domain: 10,000 emails a day; custom domain: 50,000.
  • Customer Voice is not Voice of the Customer (a solution whose deprecation was announced in July 2019 and took effect on July 1, 2020) and not a Copilot Studio survey agent.

Personalize a survey

Variables insert custom information into survey text and invitations. Built-in variables are First Name, Last Name and locale (the survey language when it is embedded in an email; use a language code such as en or fr).

  1. Open the survey → Design tab → Customization → Personalization.
  2. Select Add variable, enter a name and a default value, then Save.
  3. Insert it from the Variables list in the formatting toolbar. It appears as {{First Name}} in the text.
RuleValue
Variables per surveyMaximum 15
Variable nameUp to 30 characters, English letters and numbers only; cannot be renamed after creation
Personalized data per variableName plus value up to 1,600 characters
Where you can use themSurvey description, question text and subtitle, section heading and description, post-survey message, branching rules, invitation emails, embedded surveys (Likert questions: type the name by hand)
Where values come fromDefault values in the Personalization panel; CSV columns (override the defaults); the Send a survey action's Advanced parameters (static values or dynamic content); embed-code arguments
  • When Anonymous responses is on, variable values are not stored unless you turn on the variable's Save value toggle (off by default). Do not rely on variables in anonymous surveys: generic links and QR codes show the variable name as typed.
  • Stored values appear on the response's Personalized data tab.
  • Personalize the email: in the composer use Insert → Personalized variables (or New variable) in the subject and message, Insert → Survey link, Unsubscribe link, and First question of the survey (a Choice with a single answer, a Rating or a Net Promoter Score question that is first in the survey; not allowed when question shuffling is on).
  • Look and feel: the survey header can use a theme color, background image and logo; surveys can be multilingual; an email template can be created in each survey language.
Exam traps
  • Names: English letters and numbers only, 30 characters maximum, 15 variables per survey, no renaming.
  • Default values apply when no other value is supplied; CSV and flow values override them.
  • Anonymous responses and non-personalized links do not replace or store variables by default.
  • The locale variable takes a language code, not a language name.

Populate survey results against cases and conversations

Customer Voice invitations and responses are saved in Dataverse as user-owned activity records (the Customer Voice survey invite and survey response tables), and the docs show both on a case's timeline. What links them to a case is the Regarding value; what links them to a person is Recipient details.

InputStoresRules
RegardingThe record the invitation and response attach to (for example the case)Logical name of the table (incident for Case); only tables marked for collaboration in activities; Task not supported
Recipient detailsThe contact (stored in the invitation's To field)Contact only; needs Save invited participants as Contacts on, and the To column is not on the form by default (add it in Advanced Find)
  • Case flow: with the Support template (or any flow with Regarding set to the case), the invitation and the response appear on the case timeline; hover over the response and select Open Record to see it in the Customer Voice survey response form. A case manager can then report CSAT by case or reopen a case when the score is low.
  • Email composer and CSV: download the advanced CSV template (Import contacts → Advance options → Download advanced template) and fill RegardingID (record GUID) and RegardingEntityName (logical name) to attach each invitation to a record.
  • Send Survey command: Regarding is filled only for Account, Contact and Lead records.
  • Anonymous means unlinked people: Anonymous responses, generic links and QR codes record no name or email.
  • Conversations: the documented mechanism is the workstream's post-conversation survey. The survey and its data are not hosted or stored in Dynamics 365 Contact Center, and responses are logged as Anonymous with the respondent address anonymous-post-conversation@omnichannelengagementhub.com. That article describes no separate per-conversation linking step.
  • Data flow: a response is first stored in Customer Voice services (Microsoft-managed storage in North America or Europe), processed by Azure Cognitive Services and the Customer Voice analytics engine, then stored in your Dataverse environment. Invitation emails use the Dynamics 365 Marketing email service internally, with no Marketing subscription needed.
  • Results and follow-up: satisfaction metrics score each response; alert rules on those metrics create follow-up alerts (§3.1). Invitation statistics count Total, Responded, Not responded (Unread, Read, Opened) and Not sent.
  • Custom security roles need User-level rights on the Customer Voice tables, Read on Contact (to associate invitations) and Append To on any custom table you attach to.
Exam traps
  • Nothing shows on the case timeline unless Regarding is set (logical name incident) and the invitation is personalized.
  • Recipient details links the contact, not the case.
  • Responses to post-conversation surveys are logged as anonymous, so do not expect a named customer.
  • Refreshing or copying one Dataverse environment over another breaks Customer Voice projects and surveys in the refreshed environment, and deleting Customer Voice rows directly in Dataverse is not synchronized with the service.
  • The Send Survey command sets Regarding only for Account, Contact and Lead.

sections.title: Study habits that work
sections.html:
• Build, then read. Do the task in the product first, then read the section to see what you missed.
  • Memorize exact names: menu paths, settings, limits, roles and (for code) object, method and attribute names.
  • Practise the decision, not just the definition. For every feature write "choose it when / do not choose it when".
  • Keep a trap log. Every missed question becomes one line: what I picked and why it was wrong.
  • Use the Missed filter in Quick drill until it is empty, then re-take the full exam.
  • Read documentation dated 2026. Features were renamed and moved between preview and GA recently.

parts.subtitle: Preparation, pacing, tools allowed and break rules

sections.title: Exam-day plan
sections.html:
The week before

  • Take the full timed practice exam twice, a few days apart; fix every skill rated below 4.
  • Skim the cheat sheets and your trap log — do not start new topics.
  • Run the exam sandbox (aka.ms/examdemo) once so flagging, the review screen and the case-study layout are familiar.
  • Online exam? Run Pearson VUE's system test, clear your desk and room and have government ID ready. Test center? Confirm the address and arrival time.
  • Re-check the official study guide in case Microsoft revised the skills list.

During the exam

TopicApproach
PacingWith 40–60 questions in 100 minutes you have roughly 1.7–2.5 minutes per question. Do not spend more than about 3 minutes on one item in the first pass.
First passAnswer what you know, flag what you do not. Answer every question before time runs out — an unanswered item cannot earn credit.
EliminationCross out answers that use retired, renamed or wrong-direction features. Many questions have two plausible options — look for the deciding constraint (GA versus Preview, required role, prerequisite, order of steps).
Multi-selectCount how many answers are requested ("Select TWO"); each must be independently correct.
Configuration itemsCheck the exact setting, scope, role or sequence the requirement names before choosing between similar options.
Case studiesSkim the questions first, then read the scenario for the requirements and constraints that matter. Re-read the exhibit instead of relying on memory. Breaks are allowed in case studies, but you cannot return to questions seen before the break.
Microsoft Learn buttonOn associate and expert exams Microsoft Learn opens in a split screen (no extra time; Q&A, practice assessments and your profile are blocked). Use it only to confirm one detail with Ctrl+F; if you cannot find it in about 90 seconds, make your best choice and flag it.
BreaksThe clock keeps running during a break, and after a break you cannot go back to earlier questions. You cannot break in the middle of a lab or a problem/solution question set. Use the restroom before you start.
ReviewUse the review screen for flagged items. Change an answer only if you can name the specific fact that makes your first choice wrong.

Sources: Exam duration and experience · Retake policy.
